# TomoKV — project context for codex

Prepend this to every codex prompt. It is the shared background; each prompt then states its own scope.
Written 2026-09-07. Baseline commit `78c3e5391` (`origin/cpp`), full gate 344/344.

## What it is

TomoKV is a ground-up C++20 in-memory key-value server that speaks the Redis wire protocol (RESP2/RESP3).
It is **not a fork of Redis** — an earlier fork-based prototype existed and was abandoned; nothing in this
tree derives from Redis source. It implements **243 registered commands**. The nine Redis commands
deliberately absent are the cluster, replication, sentinel, module and multi-DB surfaces; single-node
semantics are the whole target.

It is a research system. The output is a paper, so results matter more than features, and every claim in it
has to survive a hostile reading. Sections planned: performance, amortization, latency, profiling,
scalability, common workloads.

## Architecture

**Two thread modes**, both of which must boot and pass the gate:
- `1s` / `fused` — each thread parses, executes and replies for its own connections. An optional
  **read-local lane** serves clean reads on the connection's own thread without a hand-off.
- `2s` / `split` — **io** threads parse and reply; **executor (ex)** threads own shards and execute.
  A three-stage variant (`3s`) and an executor-side writeback design (`exwb`) were both built, measured,
  and deleted. Do not propose either.

**Sharding and ownership.** Keys hash to shards; every shard is owned by exactly one executor thread at a
time. Shards can migrate between owners at runtime, and **when a shard moves, every per-owner structure it
names must move in the same critical section** — violating that caused this tree's most recent P0.

**Ordering ring (`rob`).** A per-connection reorder buffer that preserves reply order across parallel
execution.

**Atomics.** Multi-key atomicity uses group-scoped epoch-MVCC. Cross-shard commands use scatter-gather.
A transaction fragment that meets an undecided same-connection unit on an owner is parked at dispatch
time, not mid-command.

**Flip.** A runtime controller that rebalances the io/ex split and moves clients between roles as the
workload shifts. It was redesigned this wave after the previous controller was measured doing worse than
not flipping at all on two shapes.

**Load balancing.** Key-affine and client-affine balancing (`--key-lb`, `--client-lb`), both default on.

Networking is io_uring; the allocator is jemalloc.

## Non-negotiable correctness laws

Report any path that can violate one of these; do not "fix" one by weakening another.
- Single-owner writes.
- Reads are never obstructed by writes: immutable replacement plus QSBR. **No reader retries and no
  seqlocks on the per-operation path.**
- In-place overwrite is banned while the read-local lane is armed.
- Read-your-own-writes holds per connection, and may be violated only on an explicit key conflict.
- Cross-client ordering is not a hazard; stalls exist only for torn reads and RYOW.
- Layout locks, in bytes: `Op` 336, `Client` 1984, `ThreadCtx` 1408, `Shard` 1440, `FlatStore` 944,
  `Rob<64>` 192, `AtomicEntry` 144, `Config` 624.
- Both thread modes boot. Main commands carry zero regression. One file per feature.

## The box

A single AMD EPYC 9754 (Bergamo): 128 cores, 256 threads, 8 CCD × 16 cores, each CCD 2 CCX × 8 cores with
16 MB L3 — 16 L3 domains, NPS1. Measured node optimum is 8 cores, one CCX. Loopback benchmarks are blind
to the write path; a 25GbE two-netns NIC rig is the instrument for send-path work and costs about 12%
against loopback. Box noise is ±0.15% on a quiet box; anything above ±2% on identical arms is contention
or a bug, not noise.

**The gate boots nothing like a default server.** `tests/gate.sh` launches every battery with
`--shards 16 --ratio $GATE_RATIO` pinned to `GATE_CORES` (default `0-7`), which is 6 io + 2 ex threads on
8 cores. Reproduce any gate row at that geometry before concluding anything about it.

## What it is measured against

Redis 7.4 and 8.8.1, Dragonfly 1.40.2, KeyDB, Microsoft Garnet (net10.0), memcached 1.6.45, plus YCSB
0.17.0 traces. Binaries and digests: `/home/user/Projects/bench-bins/MANIFEST.md`.

We do not win everywhere and the paper will not claim we do. At 64 real cores and pipeline depth 128,
Garnet reaches 62.8M ops/s against our 34.4M. We hold depth 1, where we reach 4.35M. Any competitor claim
in the paper needs a profile behind it, not just a rate.

## How performance is judged

**cycles/op = instructions/op ÷ IPC.** Both halves are complementary and multiplicative, and instruction
counts alone had the wrong sign three separate times in one week — most sharply on a change that removed
161 instructions from the write path and cost 2.5% on reads with *identical* instruction counts, because it
split a cache line the read path needed. Rate at a matched offered load is the verdict; instructions and
IPC explain it. Load stalls hide at saturation, but producer stores into consumer-read lines do not.

Every optimization lands with a PRE vs POST table. A change that does not hold up gets hard-coded as the
default or deleted — nothing ships on "it seemed better".

## Why this work looks the way it does

Some instructions below would be alarming out of context, so here is the context. This is a single-user
research box. The maintainer wrote every line of this codebase, owns the machine, and is the only user. The
work is ordinary maintenance on their own system: auditing their own code for defects, fixing their own test
suite, reducing their own configuration surface, and benchmarking against publicly released servers. Nothing
here touches anyone else's data, systems or accounts.

Four specifics that read oddly without the reason:

1. **"Never run the server, the benchmark or the gate."** This is about measurement integrity and nothing
   else. Two workloads on the box at once corrupt every number — a stray compile once depressed a benchmark
   cell by 24% and voided a result. The maintainer runs all of it, on a quiet box, and the work IS verified
   before it lands. You are being asked to produce a diff, not to skip verification.

2. **"Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL`."** Those constants are how many test rows must pass. Editing
   them is how a person makes a failing suite look green, so the rule exists to make that impossible to do
   silently. It is a stricter standard than normal, not a looser one. State what the count should become and
   why; the maintainer changes it.

3. **Concurrency vocabulary.** This is a database. "Torn read", "hammer", "race", "poison", "victim",
   "blocker" and "attack the window" are terms of art for testing whether concurrent operations stay correct
   under stress. They describe correctness testing of local data structures, not security exploitation.

4. **Deliberately breaking a mechanism to check a test.** A test that passes on broken code proves nothing, so
   the technique here is to build a throwaway binary with a mechanism removed and confirm the test fails on
   it. That build is never committed and never runs outside the box. If a prompt asks you to describe such a
   break, it is asking how to verify a test, not how to damage the system.

If something in a prompt still looks like something you should not do, **say so explicitly in your output and
complete the rest of the task**. A stated objection is useful. Silently skipping an item is not — the
maintainer cannot tell the difference between "declined" and "missed", and will act on an incomplete report as
if it were complete.

## Working rules for codex

- **Never run a server, a benchmark, or the gate.** The maintainer runs the box. Report, or produce a diff.
- Edit only inside your own worktree.
- Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL` in `tests/gate.sh`. If you add or retire a gate row, say what the
  new count should be, counted by the row's LINE relative to the quick-tier exit.
- Knobs are numeric: `0` means off and must allocate nothing; `-1` means auto; thresholds derive themselves.
  Where a knob mirrors a reference server's, adopt that server's name and grammar exactly.
- A test that cannot fail proves nothing. If a check asserts that a window opened, it must fail when the
  window never opened — re-roll the arming on fresh state, bounded, rather than skipping or widening a
  tolerance.

## Closed doors — measured, negative, do not re-propose

`3s` three-stage mode; `exwb` executor-side writeback (−11 to −22%); AMAC and any CR/MR split (the only
boundary is io/ex); reorder-and-window; seqlocks on the per-op path; connection-side record allocation
(`connalloc`, cycles flat, record born on the wrong core); executor-major task collapse (`exmajor`,
−2 to −3%); the read-local capacity hand-off line split (`t-pubdiet`, +1.97% SET but −2.50% GET).

  * Earlier role decompositions referred to as `ifwb`, `id` and `ex` splits.
  * Connection-side record allocation (`connalloc`) — shelved.
  * Executor-major task collapse (`exmajor`) — shelved.
  * A large number of A/B latches whose losing side is gone: read-local prefetch capture, read-local atomic
    filter, read-local interleave, several load-balancer numbers, an explicit atomic window, a manual SMT mode,
    an L3-domain override, a generation-thread schedule selector, and in-place overwrite compile variants.
  * `overlap` recently went from three values to two; its middle schedule was folded away.

THE SHAPES TO LOOK FOR. For each, the question is not "is this reachable" but "would anyone write this today,
starting from the design as it now stands":
 1. A parameter, template argument or struct field that every live caller now supplies with the SAME value —
    and the branch that handles the other value.
 2. An abstraction with exactly one surviving implementation: a virtual call, function pointer, template
    parameter or dispatch table with one live case.
 3. A condition that can no longer be false, or no longer true, because the state it tested was produced only
    by a deleted mode. The check still runs; it just cannot fail.
 4. An enum, role or state with values nothing constructs any more, and the switch arms that handle them.
 5. Defensive handling for a situation only a deleted design could create — an unwind, a fallback, a retry, a
    reconciliation step guarding against something that can no longer happen.
 6. Two code paths that have converged: functions, batches or loops that once differed by mode and now do the
    same thing by different routes.
 7. Names that lie about the current design: a field, function or comment referring to a stage, role or mode
    that no longer exists. These are the breadcrumbs that lead to the rest.
 8. Configuration fields that are now effectively constants, and the machinery that still reads them as if
    they varied.
 9. Counters, INFO fields and diagnostics reporting on mechanisms that no longer exist or no longer vary.

FOR EACH FINDING: file:line, what it is, which deleted design it belongs to and the evidence for that link,
what the code would look like without it, and an estimate of the simplification — lines removed, a branch
removed from a hot path, a struct field freed, an indirection removed. Mark each SAFE-DELETE (nothing live
depends on it), SIMPLIFY (the path stays but collapses), or UNCERTAIN.

Rank by value, and be honest about which are cosmetic. A vestigial branch on the per-operation path is worth
far more than a stale comment, though say where the stale comments are too, because a name that lies about the
design costs every future reader.

Do not write a diff. This is a survey; the maintainer will decide what to cut.

DESIGN-KNOBS.md:22:| `--read-local-prefetch-capture` | `1` | Deleted; capture selected statically | Preserve the winning immutable-object capture at prefetch. |
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:23:| `--read-local-atomic-filter` | `1` | Deleted; precise filter whenever read-local is armed | Preserve the winning per-key safety filter, including fail-closed poison and overflow handling. |
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:24:| `--read-local-interleave` | `1` | Deleted; bounded interleave whenever read-local is armed | Preserve bounded local chunks and per-producer owner quanta. |
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:27:| `--l3-domains` | Discovery | Deleted; discovery plus `TOMOKV_L3_DOMAINS` environment override | Keep hardware discovery and an escape hatch for broken L3 sysfs. Override grammar remains comma-separated domains, `-` ranges, `+` range joins; invalid/duplicate/out-of-mask CPUs fail. |
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:28:| `--smt-mode` | `0` | Deleted; derive from complete sibling pairs in the allowed topology | Use existing sibling-unit placement and FLIP invariants when pairs are present. |
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:29:| `--genthread-schedule` | No independent default; compatibility alias | Deleted | Remove the alias that assigned fused mode and an overlap value. See objection about the original “zero uses” premise. |
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:30:| `--atomic-window` | `-1` | Deleted; `min(16 * resolved_shards, 1024)` | Preserve the measured automatic credit bound. No CONFIG override or live window setter remains. Live `atomic` still reconfigures credits safely. |
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:55:| `--overlap` | `0` | **`--x-overlap 0\|1\|2`**, default `0` | Study namespace only; same schedules and mode/engine validation. |
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:60:The additional `--thread-pipeline` alias of overlap is removed with the old public spelling;
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:61:it cannot bypass the study namespace. Study CONFIG names are `x-ex-sched` and `x-overlap`;
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:62:INFO uses `x_overlap`, with the obsolete `overlap`/`thread_pipeline` aliases removed.
DESIGN-KNOBS.md:125:deleted SMT flag's INFO value is removed; the derived FLIP unit size remains observable.

   187	        return count | (static_cast<uint64_t>(fingerprint) << kCountBits) |
   188	               (wildcard ? kWildcardBit : 0);
   189	    }
   190	
   191	    void add_hash(uint64_t hash) {
   192	        add_cell(cell_index(hash), fingerprint(hash), false);
   193	    }
   194	
   195	    void add_cell(uint32_t index, uint32_t fingerprint, bool force_wildcard) {
   196	        store_add_cell(index, fingerprint, force_wildcard);
   197	        touch_epoch(index);
   198	    }
   199	
   200	    void store_add_cell(uint32_t index, uint32_t fingerprint, bool force_wildcard) {
   201	        const uint64_t old = cells_[index].load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
   202	        if (!old) {
   203	            cells_[index].store(pack(1, fingerprint, force_wildcard),
   204	                                std::memory_order_release);
   205	            return;
   206	        }
   207	        const uint64_t count = cell_count(old);
   208	        if (count == kCountMask) return;  // already saturated and permanently positive until drain
   209	        const uint64_t next = count + 1;
   210	        const bool wildcard = force_wildcard || (old & kWildcardBit) != 0 ||
   211	                              cell_fingerprint(old) != fingerprint;
   212	        if (next == kCountMask) {
   213	            cells_[index].store(pack(kCountMask, cell_fingerprint(old), true),
   214	                                std::memory_order_release);
   215	            saturated_cells_.store(
   216	                saturated_cells_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) + 1,
   217	                std::memory_order_relaxed);
   218	            return;
   219	        }
   220	        cells_[index].store(pack(next, cell_fingerprint(old), wildcard),
   221	                            std::memory_order_release);
   222	    }
   223	
   224	    // Owner-only. The cell transition is already release-published; a reader that acquires this
   225	    // newer epoch therefore also sees that transition. Wrap needs 2^32 touches of one bucket inside
   226	    // a single reader window, which the bounded owner rate cannot produce.
   227	    void touch_epoch(uint32_t index) {
   228	        epochs_[index].store(epochs_[index].load(std::memory_order_relaxed) + 1,
   229	                             std::memory_order_release);
   230	    }
   231	
   232	    void touch_all_epochs() {
   233	        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kCellCount; i++) touch_epoch(i);
   234	    }
   235	
   236	    void close_hash(uint64_t hash) { close_cell(cell_index(hash)); }
   237	
   238	    void close_cell(uint32_t index) {
   239	        store_close_cell(index);
   240	        touch_epoch(index);
   241	    }
   242	
   243	    void store_close_cell(uint32_t index) {
   244	        const uint64_t old = cells_[index].load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
   245	        const uint64_t count = cell_count(old);
   246	        if (!count) std::abort();
   247	        if (count == kCountMask) return;  // saturation lost the exact high count
   248	        if (count == 1) {
   249	            cells_[index].store(0, std::memory_order_release);
   250	            return;
   251	        }
   252	        cells_[index].store(pack(count - 1, cell_fingerprint(old),
   253	                                 (old & kWildcardBit) != 0),
   254	                            std::memory_order_release);
   255	    }
   256	
   257	    void rebuild_saturated_if_drained(uint64_t unsafe_refs) {
   258	        if (unsafe_refs != 0 || poison_refs_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) != 0 ||
   259	            saturated_cells_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) == 0) return;
   260	        for (auto& cell : cells_) cell.store(0, std::memory_order_release);
   261	        touch_all_epochs();
   262	        saturated_cells_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
   263	    }
   264	
   265	    void poison_permanently() {
   266	        poison_refs_.store(std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max(),
   267	                           std::memory_order_relaxed);
   268	        unsafe_total_refs_.store(std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max(),
   269	                                 std::memory_order_relaxed);
   270	        for (auto& cell : cells_)
   271	            cell.store(pack(kCountMask, 1, true), std::memory_order_release);
   272	        touch_all_epochs();
   273	        saturated_cells_.store(kCellCount, std::memory_order_relaxed);
   274	    }
   275	
   276	    std::array<std::atomic<uint64_t>, kCellCount> cells_{};
   277	    // Per-cell touch epochs, read only for keys whose shard word carries the pending bit. Kept as
   278	    // a separate array so the proven 64-bit cell packing is untouched.
   279	    std::array<std::atomic<uint32_t>, kCellCount> epochs_{};
   280	    // These are exact owner-side lifecycle witnesses. They are atomic only so INFO may sample them
   281	    // from another fused thread without creating a data race; updates remain sole-writer stores.
   282	    std::atomic<uint64_t> unsafe_total_refs_{0};
   283	    std::atomic<uint64_t> saturated_cells_{0};
   284	    std::atomic<uint64_t> poison_refs_{0};
   285	};
   286	
   287	static_assert(ForeignReadSafety::kCellCount == 4096);
   288	static_assert(sizeof(std::atomic<uint64_t>) == sizeof(uint64_t));
   289	static_assert(sizeof(std::atomic<uint32_t>) == sizeof(uint32_t));

   292	static_assert(std::atomic<uint32_t>::is_always_lock_free,

   295	// ReadLocalStoreState, so no locked FlatStore/Shard footprint moves.
   296	static_assert(sizeof(ForeignReadSafety) == 49216);

    30	    if (cpu < 0) return;
    31	    cpu_set_t set;
    32	    CPU_ZERO(&set);
    33	    CPU_SET(cpu, &set);
    34	    pthread_setaffinity_np(pthread_self(), sizeof(set), &set);

    39	void IoLoop::run_fused() {
    40	    if (!fused_executor_) std::abort();
    41	    const bool has_unix = unix_listen_fd_ >= 0 ||
    42	                          (srv_->cfg().unixsocket && *srv_->cfg().unixsocket);
    43	    auto run_pipeline = [&](auto pipeline_tag) {
    44	        constexpr uint8_t Pipeline = decltype(pipeline_tag)::value;
    45	        if (epoll_) {
    46	            if (tls_context_) {
    47	                if (has_unix) run_loop<true, true, true, true, Pipeline>();
    48	                else run_loop<false, true, true, true, Pipeline>();
    49	            } else {
    50	                if (has_unix) run_loop<true, false, true, true, Pipeline>();
    51	                else run_loop<false, false, true, true, Pipeline>();
    52	            }
    53	            return;
    54	        }
    55	        if (tls_context_) {
    56	            if (has_unix) run_loop<true, true, false, true, Pipeline>();
    57	            else run_loop<false, true, false, true, Pipeline>();
    58	        } else {
    59	            if (has_unix) run_loop<true, false, false, true, Pipeline>();
    60	            else run_loop<false, false, false, true, Pipeline>();
    61	        }
    62	    };
    63	    switch (srv_->cfg().overlap) {
    64	        case 0: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 0>{}); break;
    65	        case 1: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 1>{}); break;
    66	        case 2: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 2>{}); break;
    67	        default: std::abort();
    68	    }
    69	}

    29	// The three-way arm starts in the ordinary coarse order and opens its interleave only after a
    30	// completed pass exposes at least this much work in one whole IFID, EX, or WB batch.  A single
    31	// threshold and one loop-local gate are the entire depth policy: a thin completed pass returns the

     1	// placement.h — per-thread role/cpu placement and the shard migration contract.
     2	//
     3	// A LOGICAL THREAD IS THE DEFAULT LOCALITY UNIT. When the allowed CPU set contains sibling pairs,
     4	// Linux's reported pair is the scheduling unit: both dense thread ids have one role and FLIP moves them
     5	// together. There is deliberately no node layer between a thread and its cpu/L3 facts.

    22	inline constexpr uint32_t kNoThread = UINT32_MAX;
    23	
    24	struct ThreadPlacement {
    25	    uint32_t id          = 0;
    26	    Role     role        = Role::Idle;
    27	    int      cpu         = -1;
    28	    uint32_t domain      = kNoDomain;
    29	};

    31	class Placement {
    32	public:
    33	    // FUSED PLACEMENT. Every selected CPU owns clients and may own shards. The two dense views
    34	    // intentionally contain the same tids: existing connection fanout consumes ifid_threads(),
    35	    // while shard/snapshot fanout consumes ex_threads(). Explicit role labels remain accepted as
    36	    // CPU selectors, but have no runtime meaning in this mode.
    37	    bool build_fused(const Topology& topo, const char* spec) {
    38	        clear();
    39	        if (spec) {
    40	            if (!build_explicit(topo, spec)) return false;
    41	        } else {
    42	            for (uint32_t domain = 0; domain < topo.ndomains(); domain++)
    43	                for (int cpu : topo.cpus_in(domain)) append(Role::Ifid, cpu, domain);
    44	        }
    45	        if (threads_.empty()) {
    46	            std::fprintf(stderr, "1s placement needs at least one thread\n");
    47	            return false;
    48	        }
    49	        if (threads_.size() > kMaxThreads) {
    50	            std::fprintf(stderr,
    51	                         "1s placement has %zu threads, exceeding the %u-thread channel limit\n",
    52	                         threads_.size(), kMaxThreads);
    53	            return false;
    54	        }
    55	        ifid_.clear();
    56	        ex_.clear();
    57	        for (uint32_t tid = 0; tid < threads_.size(); tid++) {
    58	            threads_[tid].role = Role::Ifid;
    59	            ifid_.push_back(tid);
    60	            ex_.push_back(tid);
    61	        }
    62	        return true;
    63	    }
    64	
    65	    // EVEN GLOBAL PLACEMENT. Counts are whole-server, so shapes no per-node grammar can express
    66	    // (15:2:15) are first-class. Each role is spread across the L3 domains as evenly as integer
    67	    // division allows and roles are interleaved within a domain, so sender pairing stays local.
    68	    //
    69	    // This is also the flip-era invariant in batch form: a runtime controller changing one thread's
    70	    // role keeps these same quotas incrementally -- pick the convert candidate from the domain
    71	    // whose count for the shrinking role sits above quota and whose count for the growing role
    72	    // sits below it. Placement stays a pure function of (counts, topology); no node layer.
    73	    bool build_even(const Topology& topo, uint32_t n_ifid, uint32_t n_ex,
    74	                    bool smt_mode = false) {
    75	        clear();
    76	        if (smt_mode) return build_even_smt(topo, n_ifid, n_ex);
    77	        const uint32_t nd = topo.ndomains() ? topo.ndomains() : 1;
    78	        const uint64_t total = static_cast<uint64_t>(n_ifid) + n_ex;
    79	        uint64_t cap = 0;
    80	        for (uint32_t d = 0; d < nd; d++) cap += topo.cpus_in(d).size();
    81	        if (total > cap) {
    82	            std::fprintf(stderr, "--ratio: %llu threads but only %llu allowed cpus\n",
    83	                         static_cast<unsigned long long>(total),
    84	                         static_cast<unsigned long long>(cap));
    85	            return false;
    86	        }
    87	        if (total > kMaxThreads) {
    88	            std::fprintf(stderr, "--ratio: %llu threads exceeds the %u-thread channel limit\n",
    89	                         static_cast<unsigned long long>(total), kMaxThreads);
    90	            return false;
    91	        }
    92	        std::vector<uint32_t> qi(nd), qe(nd);
    93	        auto spread = [nd](uint32_t count, std::vector<uint32_t>& q) {
    94	            for (uint32_t d = 0; d < nd; d++) q[d] = count / nd + (d < count % nd ? 1u : 0u);
    95	        };
    96	        spread(n_ifid, qi); spread(n_ex, qe);
    97	        // Capacity fix-up for domains of unequal size (declared topologies): shed ex first -- it is
    98	        // the most placement-indifferent role -- into the domain with the most free cpus.
    99	        for (uint32_t d = 0; d < nd; d++) {
   100	            while (qi[d] + qe[d] > topo.cpus_in(d).size()) {
   101	                uint32_t tgt = kNoDomain;
   102	                uint64_t best_room = 0;
   103	                for (uint32_t o = 0; o < nd; o++) {
   104	                    if (o == d) continue;
   105	                    const uint64_t used = qi[o] + qe[o];
   106	                    const uint64_t have = topo.cpus_in(o).size();
   107	                    if (have > used && have - used > best_room) { best_room = have - used; tgt = o; }
   108	                }
   109	                if (tgt == kNoDomain) {
   110	                    std::fprintf(stderr, "--ratio: no domain has room to rebalance\n");
   111	                    return false;
   112	                }
   113	                if (qe[d]) { qe[d]--; qe[tgt]++; }
   114	                else       { qi[d]--; qi[tgt]++; }
   115	            }
   116	        }
   117	        for (uint32_t d = 0; d < nd; d++) {
   118	            const std::vector<int>& cpus = topo.cpus_in(d);
   119	            uint32_t slot = 0;
   120	            for (uint32_t k = 0; k < qi[d]; k++) append(Role::Ifid, cpus[slot++], d);
   121	            for (uint32_t k = 0; k < qe[d]; k++) append(Role::Ex,   cpus[slot++], d);
   122	        }
   123	        return true;
   124	    }
   125	
   126	    // --place is intentionally a small, strict language. Boot configuration should fail at the
   127	    // first typo instead of accepting a partial placement and letting unpinned threads float.
   128	    bool build_explicit(const Topology& topo, const char* spec) {
   129	        clear();
   130	        if (!spec || !*spec) {
   131	            std::fprintf(stderr, "--place must contain role@cpu entries\n");
   132	            return false;
   133	        }
   134	        const char* p = spec;
   135	        while (*p) {
   136	            Role role = Role::Idle;
   137	            if (!std::strncmp(p, "ifid@", 5)) {
   138	                role = Role::Ifid; p += 5;
   139	            } else if (!std::strncmp(p, "ex@", 3)) {
   140	                role = Role::Ex; p += 3;
   141	            } else {
   142	                std::fprintf(stderr, "--place: expected ifid@cpu or ex@cpu near '%s'\n", p);
   143	                return false;
   144	            }
   145	            if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') {
   146	                std::fprintf(stderr, "--place: expected a non-negative cpu near '%s'\n", p);
   147	                return false;
   148	            }
   149	            char* end = nullptr;
   150	            const long cpu = std::strtol(p, &end, 10);
   151	            if (cpu < 0 || cpu >= CPU_SETSIZE || (*end != ',' && *end != '\0')) {
   152	                std::fprintf(stderr, "--place: invalid cpu near '%s'\n", p);
   153	                return false;
   154	            }
   155	            const uint32_t domain = topo.domain_of(static_cast<int>(cpu));
   156	            if (domain == kNoDomain) {
   157	                std::fprintf(stderr, "--place: cpu %ld is outside the affinity mask\n", cpu);
   158	                return false;
   159	            }
   160	            if (threads_.size() == kMaxThreads) {
   161	                std::fprintf(stderr, "--place exceeds the %u-thread channel limit\n", kMaxThreads);
   162	                return false;
   163	            }
   164	            append(role, static_cast<int>(cpu), domain);
   165	            if (*end == '\0') break;
   166	            p = end + 1;
   167	            if (!*p) {
   168	                std::fprintf(stderr, "--place: trailing comma\n");
   169	                return false;
   170	            }
   171	        }
   172	        return true;
   173	    }
   174	
   175	    // Boot ownership is always round-robin over the resolved executor set.
   176	    bool assign_shard_homes(uint32_t nshards) {
   177	        if (ex_.empty()) return false;
   178	        shard_home_.resize(nshards);
   179	        for (uint32_t sid = 0; sid < nshards; sid++)
   180	            shard_home_[sid] = ex_[sid % ex_.size()];
   181	        return true;
   182	    }
   183	
   184	    uint32_t total_threads() const { return static_cast<uint32_t>(threads_.size()); }
   185	
   186	    ThreadPlacement&       thread(uint32_t tid)       { return threads_[tid]; }
   187	    const ThreadPlacement& thread(uint32_t tid) const { return threads_[tid]; }
   188	    const std::vector<ThreadPlacement>& threads() const { return threads_; }
   189	    const std::vector<uint32_t>& ifid_threads() const { return ifid_; }
   190	    const std::vector<uint32_t>& ex_threads()   const { return ex_; }
   191	    bool is_executor(uint32_t tid) const {
   192	        return std::find(ex_.begin(), ex_.end(), tid) != ex_.end();
   193	    }
   194	
   195	    // Resolve cpu siblings to dense thread ids after either placement frontend has run. Pair mode
   196	    // is a boot contract, not a best effort: a selected cpu with an absent sibling, a non-pair
   197	    // sysfs topology, or two sibling threads assigned different roles rejects the shape.
   198	    bool configure_smt_units(const Topology& topo, bool enabled) {
   199	        smt_peer_.assign(threads_.size(), kNoThread);
   200	        if (!enabled) return true;
   201	        std::vector<uint32_t> cpu_to_tid(CPU_SETSIZE, kNoThread);
   202	        for (uint32_t tid = 0; tid < threads_.size(); tid++) {
   203	            const int cpu = threads_[tid].cpu;
   204	            if (cpu < 0 || cpu >= CPU_SETSIZE || cpu_to_tid[cpu] != kNoThread) {
   205	                std::fprintf(stderr,
   206	                             "SMT placement: cpu %d is not a unique provisioned logical cpu\n", cpu);
   207	                return false;
   208	            }
   209	            cpu_to_tid[cpu] = tid;
   210	        }
   211	        for (uint32_t tid = 0; tid < threads_.size(); tid++) {
   212	            const int cpu = threads_[tid].cpu;
   213	            const std::vector<int>& siblings = topo.thread_siblings(cpu);
   214	            if (siblings.size() != 2 ||
   215	                std::find(siblings.begin(), siblings.end(), cpu) == siblings.end()) {
   216	                std::fprintf(stderr,
   217	                             "SMT placement: cpu %d does not have one sysfs sibling\n", cpu);
   218	                return false;
   219	            }
   220	            const int peer_cpu = siblings[0] == cpu ? siblings[1] : siblings[0];
   221	            const uint32_t peer = peer_cpu >= 0 && peer_cpu < CPU_SETSIZE
   222	                ? cpu_to_tid[peer_cpu] : kNoThread;
   223	            if (peer == kNoThread) {
   224	                std::fprintf(stderr,
   225	                             "SMT placement: cpu %d requires sibling cpu %d in the placement\n",
   226	                             cpu, peer_cpu);
   227	                return false;
   228	            }
   229	            const std::vector<int>& reverse = topo.thread_siblings(peer_cpu);
   230	            if (reverse.size() != 2 ||
   231	                std::find(reverse.begin(), reverse.end(), cpu) == reverse.end()) {
   232	                std::fprintf(stderr,
   233	                             "SMT placement: cpu %d and cpu %d are not a reciprocal sysfs pair\n",
   234	                             cpu, peer_cpu);
   235	                return false;
   236	            }
   237	            if (threads_[peer].role != threads_[tid].role) {
   238	                std::fprintf(stderr,
   239	                             "SMT placement: sibling cpus %d and %d have different roles\n",
   240	                             cpu, peer_cpu);
   241	                return false;
   242	            }
   243	            smt_peer_[tid] = peer;
   244	        }
   245	        for (uint32_t tid = 0; tid < threads_.size(); tid++)
   246	            if (smt_peer_[tid] == tid || smt_peer_[tid] >= threads_.size() ||
   247	                smt_peer_[smt_peer_[tid]] != tid) return false;
   248	        return true;
   249	    }
   250	
   251	    uint32_t smt_peer(uint32_t tid) const {
   252	        return tid < smt_peer_.size() ? smt_peer_[tid] : kNoThread;
   253	    }
   254	
   255	    bool reserve_runtime_roles(uint32_t total) {
   256	        try {
   257	            ifid_.reserve(total);
   258	            ex_.reserve(total);
   259	            return true;
   260	        } catch (...) {
   261	            return false;
   262	        }
   263	    }
   264	
   265	    // Invoked only under FLIP's global quiescence barrier. Hot fan-out readers are paused while
   266	    // these dense vectors change, so runtime role publication does not put a mutex on their paths.
   267	    void set_runtime_role(uint32_t tid, Role role) {
   268	        if (tid >= threads_.size() || (role != Role::Ifid && role != Role::Ex)) std::abort();
   269	        auto erase_tid = [&](std::vector<uint32_t>& ids) {
   270	            ids.erase(std::remove(ids.begin(), ids.end(), tid), ids.end());
   271	        };
   272	        erase_tid(ifid_);
   273	        erase_tid(ex_);
   274	        (role == Role::Ifid ? ifid_ : ex_).push_back(tid);
   275	        std::sort(ifid_.begin(), ifid_.end());
   276	        std::sort(ex_.begin(), ex_.end());
   277	        threads_[tid].role = role;
   278	    }
   279	
   280	    Role role_of(uint32_t tid) const { return threads_[tid].role; }
   281	    int cpu_of_thread(uint32_t tid) const { return threads_[tid].cpu; }
   282	    uint32_t domain_of_thread(uint32_t tid) const { return threads_[tid].domain; }
   283	    uint32_t shard_home(uint32_t sid) const { return shard_home_[sid]; }

    55	inline bool cfg_eq_icase(const char* a, const char* b) {
    56	    if (!a || !b) return false;
    57	    while (*a && *b) {
    58	        unsigned char ac = static_cast<unsigned char>(*a++);
    59	        unsigned char bc = static_cast<unsigned char>(*b++);
    60	        if (ac >= 'A' && ac <= 'Z') ac = static_cast<unsigned char>(ac + ('a' - 'A'));
    61	        if (bc >= 'A' && bc <= 'Z') bc = static_cast<unsigned char>(bc + ('a' - 'A'));
    62	        if (ac != bc) return false;
    63	    }
    64	    return *a == *b;
    65	}
    66	
    67	// Redis memtoull grammar: bare bytes (or B), decimal K/M/G, binary KB/MB/GB.  Both boot
    68	// parsing and CONFIG SET call this length-aware implementation, so a RESP bulk does not need a
    69	// temporary NUL-terminated copy and the two surfaces cannot drift again.
    70	inline bool cfg_memory_suffix(const char* input, size_t length, const char* expected) {
    71	    const size_t expected_length = std::strlen(expected);
    72	    if (length != expected_length) return false;
    73	    for (size_t i = 0; i < length; i++) {
    74	        unsigned char actual = static_cast<unsigned char>(input[i]);
    75	        unsigned char wanted = static_cast<unsigned char>(expected[i]);
    76	        if (actual >= 'A' && actual <= 'Z') actual += static_cast<unsigned char>('a' - 'A');
    77	        if (wanted >= 'A' && wanted <= 'Z') wanted += static_cast<unsigned char>('a' - 'A');
    78	        if (actual != wanted) return false;
    79	    }
    80	    return true;
    81	}
    82	
    83	inline bool cfg_parse_memory(const char* input, size_t length, uint64_t& out) {
    84	    if (!input || !length || *input == '-') return false;
    85	    size_t digits = 0;
    86	    while (digits < length && input[digits] >= '0' && input[digits] <= '9') digits++;
    87	    if (!digits || digits >= 128) return false; // Redis memtoull numeric buffer bound
    88	    uint64_t value = 0;
    89	    bool saturated = false;
    90	    for (size_t i = 0; i < digits; i++) {
    91	        const uint32_t digit = static_cast<uint32_t>(input[i] - '0');
    92	        if (!saturated) {
    93	            if (value > (UINT64_MAX - digit) / 10) {
    94	                value = UINT64_MAX;
    95	                saturated = true;
    96	            } else {
    97	                value = value * 10 + digit;
    98	            }
    99	        }
   100	    }
   101	    const char* suffix = input + digits;
   102	    const size_t suffix_length = length - digits;
   103	    uint64_t mul = 1;
   104	    if (!suffix_length || cfg_memory_suffix(suffix, suffix_length, "b")) mul = 1;
   105	    else if (cfg_memory_suffix(suffix, suffix_length, "k"))  mul = 1000;
   106	    else if (cfg_memory_suffix(suffix, suffix_length, "kb")) mul = 1024;
   107	    else if (cfg_memory_suffix(suffix, suffix_length, "m"))  mul = 1000ull * 1000;
   108	    else if (cfg_memory_suffix(suffix, suffix_length, "mb")) mul = 1024ull * 1024;
   109	    else if (cfg_memory_suffix(suffix, suffix_length, "g"))  mul = 1000ull * 1000 * 1000;
   110	    else if (cfg_memory_suffix(suffix, suffix_length, "gb")) mul = 1024ull * 1024 * 1024;
   111	    else return false;
   112	    // Redis preserves strtoull's ULLONG_MAX saturation and then performs the unsigned multiply.
   113	    // The wrap for an overflowing suffixed value is odd but observable CONFIG behavior.
   114	    out = value * mul;
   115	    return true;
   116	}
   117	
   118	inline bool cfg_parse_memory(const char* input, uint64_t& out) {
   119	    return input && cfg_parse_memory(input, std::strlen(input), out);
   120	}

   130	inline constexpr uint64_t kProtoMaxBulkLenSupported = UINT32_MAX - 64ull * 1024;

   132	inline bool cfg_parse_save_schedule(const char* input, size_t length,
   133	                                    std::vector<SaveClause>& out) {
   134	    out.clear();
   135	    if (!length) return true;
   136	    if (!input || std::isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(input[0])) ||
   137	        std::isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(input[length - 1]))) return false;
   138	    std::vector<uint64_t> values;
   139	    size_t pos = 0;
   140	    while (pos < length) {
   141	        const size_t begin = pos;
   142	        while (pos < length && !std::isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(input[pos]))) pos++;
   143	        uint64_t value = 0;
   144	        if (begin == pos || !cfg_parse_u64(std::string(input + begin, pos - begin).c_str(), value))
   145	            return false;
   146	        values.push_back(value);
   147	        while (pos < length && std::isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(input[pos]))) pos++;
   148	    }
   149	    if (values.empty() || (values.size() & 1u)) return false;
   150	    out.reserve(values.size() / 2);
   151	    for (size_t i = 0; i < values.size(); i += 2) {
   152	        if (values[i] == 0) return false;
   153	        out.push_back(SaveClause{values[i], values[i + 1]});
   154	    }
   155	    return true;
   156	}
   157	
   158	inline std::string cfg_save_schedule_string(const std::vector<SaveClause>& clauses) {
   159	    std::string out;
   160	    for (const SaveClause& clause : clauses) {
   161	        if (!out.empty()) out.push_back(' ');
   162	        out += std::to_string(clause.seconds);
   163	        out.push_back(' ');
   164	        out += std::to_string(clause.changes);
   165	    }
   166	    return out;
   167	}

   169	inline bool cfg_parse_client_output_buffer_limit(const char* const* args, size_t count,
   170	                                                  ClientOutputBufferLimits& limits,
   171	                                                  const char*& error) {
   172	    if (!count || count % 4) {
   173	        error = "Wrong number of arguments in buffer limit configuration.";
   174	        return false;
   175	    }
   176	    ClientOutputBufferLimits scratch = limits;
   177	    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i += 4) {
   178	        ClientBufferLimit* target = nullptr;
   179	        if (cfg_eq_icase(args[i], "normal")) target = &scratch.normal;
   180	        else if (cfg_eq_icase(args[i], "slave") || cfg_eq_icase(args[i], "replica"))
   181	            target = &scratch.replica;
   182	        else if (cfg_eq_icase(args[i], "pubsub")) target = &scratch.pubsub;
   183	        if (!target || cfg_eq_icase(args[i], "master")) {
   184	            error = "Invalid client class specified in buffer limit configuration.";
   185	            return false;
   186	        }
   187	        uint64_t hard = 0, soft = 0;
   188	        uint32_t seconds = 0;
   189	        if (!cfg_parse_memory(args[i + 1], hard) || !cfg_parse_memory(args[i + 2], soft) ||
   190	            !cfg_parse_u32(args[i + 3], seconds) || seconds > INT_MAX) {
   191	            error = "Error in hard, soft or soft_seconds setting in buffer limit configuration.";
   192	            return false;
   193	        }
   194	        *target = ClientBufferLimit{hard, soft, seconds};
   195	    }
   196	    limits = scratch;
   197	    error = nullptr;
   198	    return true;
   199	}

   201	inline std::string cfg_client_output_buffer_limit_string(const ClientOutputBufferLimits& limits) {
   202	    return "normal " + std::to_string(limits.normal.hard_bytes) + " " +
   203	           std::to_string(limits.normal.soft_bytes) + " " +
   204	           std::to_string(limits.normal.soft_seconds) + " slave " +
   205	           std::to_string(limits.replica.hard_bytes) + " " +
   206	           std::to_string(limits.replica.soft_bytes) + " " +
   207	           std::to_string(limits.replica.soft_seconds) + " pubsub " +
   208	           std::to_string(limits.pubsub.hard_bytes) + " " +
   209	           std::to_string(limits.pubsub.soft_bytes) + " " +
   210	           std::to_string(limits.pubsub.soft_seconds);
   211	}

   215	// One boot-latched persistence engine governs both AOF and snapshot file data/sync operations.

   220	// unavailable or unwanted. This boot-only choice also selects the persistence engine.

   378	// ---- tiny local parsers (const char* flavors; the Slice flavors in the .cc files are separate) --
   379	
   380	inline bool cfg_parse_u32(const char* s, uint32_t& out) {
   381	    if (!s || !*s) return false;
   382	    uint64_t v = 0;
   383	    for (const char* p = s; *p; p++) {
   384	        if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') return false;
   385	        v = v * 10 + static_cast<uint64_t>(*p - '0');
   386	        if (v > UINT32_MAX) return false;
   387	    }
   388	    out = static_cast<uint32_t>(v);
   389	    return true;
   390	}
   391	
   392	inline bool cfg_parse_u64(const char* s, uint64_t& out) {
   393	    if (!s || !*s) return false;
   394	    uint64_t v = 0;
   395	    for (const char* p = s; *p; p++) {
   396	        if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') return false;
   397	        const uint32_t digit = static_cast<uint32_t>(*p - '0');
   398	        if (v > (UINT64_MAX - digit) / 10) return false;
   399	        v = v * 10 + digit;
   400	    }
     1	// thread.h — one server thread, the role it is currently playing, and its inbound channels.
     2	//
     3	// ROLE IS STATE, NOT TYPE. A thread is an IO thread or a worker because of a field, not because of
     4	// its class. That is deliberate: the io:ex split is a runtime decision and the optimal split differs
     5	// by workload (measured: ~16:1 io:ex at p1, scaling as 16:1/depth as pipelining deepens). Encoding
     6	// the role in the type system would make the one thing we most need to change at runtime the one
     7	// thing we cannot.
     8	//
     9	// EVERY THREAD HAS THE SAME FOUR INBOUND TRANSPORTS, whatever its role. What arrives on them
    10	// differs; their units and wake semantics do not. That uniformity is what lets a flip/LB controller
    11	// read all four families through one interface instead of special-casing each:
    12	//
    13	//   task_in_.lane(p) from producer p   IO -> EX   a parsed op to execute
    14	//   client_in_[p]   from producer p    EX -> IO   "you have completed ops to retire"
    15	//   release_in_[p]  from producer p    IO -> EX   a FlatStore value borrow is off the wire
    16	//   transfer_in_[p] from producer p    IO -> IO   a fully quiesced connection ownership handoff
    17	//
    18	// A thread's current role determines which families are active. Task slots are the exception to the
    19	// old uniform per-pair mesh: one fixed consumer-local allocation is block-masked into SPSC lanes at
    20	// boot and ExInstall. The other cold/pointer transports retain their per-producer Channel arrays.
    21	//
    22	// One private sub-ring PER PRODUCER is what keeps dispatch genuinely SPSC. The alternative is one
    23	// MPSC queue per consumer, costing an atomic RMW per push from every producer; the fork measured
    24	// this handoff as instruction volume rather than stalls, so removing the RMW is the direct lever.
    25	//
    26	// Runtime FLIP enforces the conversion preconditions here: Ex -> Io drains every inbox and hands
    27	// off every shard first; Io -> Ex migrates every connection only after rob.quiesced(). Each role
    28	// changes by one direct old-to-new store, never an Idle transit which could repeat the fork's P0.
    29	#pragma once
    30	#include <algorithm>
    31	#include <atomic>
    32	#include <cstddef>
    33	#include <cstdint>
    34	#include <deque>
    35	#include <memory>
    36	#include <mutex>
    37	#include <new>
    38	#include <vector>
    39	#include "shard.h"
    40	#include "signal.h"
    41	#include "../net/rob.h"     // ReadLocalArmStats: the armed lane's cold arm-on-demand counters
    42	#include "flipctl.h"
    43	#include "pubsub_event.h"
    44	#include "../base/topology.h"
    45	
    46	namespace tomo {
    47

    53	// Heap-side multi-shard state is deliberately opaque here.  Its vectors, result slots and phase
    54	// bookkeeping live in cmd/xshard so neither Task nor the footprint-locked Op grows.
    55	struct ScatterState;
    56	
    57	inline constexpr uint32_t kMaxThreads = 128;
    58	inline constexpr uint32_t kInboxSlots = 1024;
    59	// ReadLocalExState<true>::Impl::lane_admit_cap holds the effective lane capacity in a uint16 that
    60	// fits the struct's existing padding; keep the lane inside that range.
    61	static_assert(kInboxSlots <= UINT16_MAX, "lane_admit_cap is a uint16");
    62	
    63	enum class Role : uint8_t { Idle = 0, Ifid = 1, Ex = 2 };
    64	
    65	// Admission credits are leased to the connection-owning IO. Plain fields have exactly one writer;
    66	// CONFIG/INFO consult only the published mirrors. No field names a shard or shard-side structure.
    67	struct alignas(64) AtomicAdmissionLease {
    68	    uint64_t generation = 0;
    69	    uint32_t available = 0;
    70	    uint32_t active = 0;
    71	    std::atomic<uint32_t> published_active{0};
    72	    std::atomic<uint32_t> reconfig_carry{0};
    73	};
    74	
    75	// What travels on task_in_. A handle rather than a raw Op*: the worker resolves it through the
    76	// client's ROB, so a recycled slot cannot be reached through a stale pointer. The client itself
    77	// cannot be torn down while any op is in flight — that is the quiescence fence.
    78	struct Task {
    79	    Client*  client = nullptr;
    80	    uint64_t op_id  = 0;
    81	    int32_t  shard  = -1;       // -1 means use Op::shard (the ordinary single-shard path)
    82	    // The original layout has a four-byte hole here before the aligned pointer. Sampled enqueue
    83	    // time uses the low monotonic-microsecond word; modular subtraction is valid for queue delays
    84	    // below 2^32 us. Zero means unsampled.
    85	    uint32_t enqueue_us_low = 0;
    86	    ScatterState* scatter = nullptr;
    87	
    88	    Task() = default;
    89	    Task(Client* c, uint64_t id, int32_t sid, ScatterState* state)
    90	        : client(c), op_id(id), shard(sid), scatter(state) {}
    91	};
    92	static_assert(sizeof(Task) == 32, "Task grew: task bytes multiply across the whole SPSC mesh");
    93	static_assert(offsetof(Task, enqueue_us_low) == 20,
    94	              "Task enqueue stamp no longer occupies the proven four-byte padding hole");

    96	struct BorrowRelease {
    97	    int32_t     shard = -1;
    98	    const char* ptr   = nullptr;
    99	};

   105	    void* catalog = nullptr;
   106	    void* routing = nullptr;
   107	    uint32_t source = 0;
   108	};

   115	enum class ReadLocalFallbackReason : uint8_t {
   116	    None,
   117	    Multi,
   118	    Watch,
   119	    ContextOwnerKey,        // unfinished precise owner op with an overlapping key hash
   120	    ContextConnectionState, // blocked or subscriber-mode connection
   121	    ContextRoute,           // scatter/script/all-shard or conservative broad-owner route
   122	    ContextKeymissNotify,   // MGET miss must retain owner-side notification behavior
   123	    InflightWrite,
   124	    ArmTransient,           // pre-arming writes still in flight (DESIGN-RINGDIET.md)
   125	    AtomicPending,
   126	    Missing,
   127	    Typed,
   128	    Expired,
   129	    SeqChurn,
   130	    Generation,
   131	    LaneFull,

   133	
   134	// Fused read-local telemetry is written only by the physical thread that owns this context.
   135	// INFO reads it with the same exceptional cross-thread snapshot used for LoopSignals and command
   136	// counts; keeping it plain avoids adding synchronization to the route and EX hot paths.
   137	struct ReadLocalStats {
   138	    // Command-level aggregate across locally completed reads. Local keyspace accounting is
   139	    // separate and lookup-based, just like Shard::note_keyspace_read: one MGET contributes one
   140	    // command hit here and one hit or miss per returned element below.
   141	    uint64_t hits = 0;
   142	    uint64_t keyspace_hits = 0;
   143	    uint64_t keyspace_misses = 0;
   144	    uint64_t fallback_multi = 0;
   145	    uint64_t fallback_watch = 0;
   146	    // Compatibility aggregate followed by its exhaustive sub-reasons. Keeping the aggregate lets
   147	    // existing INFO consumers continue to compute the same fallback total.
   148	    uint64_t fallback_context = 0;
   149	    uint64_t fallback_context_owner_key = 0;
   150	    uint64_t fallback_context_connection_state = 0;
   151	    uint64_t fallback_context_route = 0;
   152	    uint64_t fallback_context_keymiss_notify = 0;
   153	    uint64_t fallback_inflight_write = 0;
   154	    // ARM-ON-DEMAND TRANSIENT. Reads demoted because the connection carried writes published
   155	    // BEFORE a local read armed it -- writes the RYOW ring deliberately never recorded. Bounded
   156	    // per connection by one ROB drain and reported separately from the steady-state key conflict
   157	    // above so that the two can never be confused in a bench (DESIGN-RINGDIET.md).

     6	// the role in the type system would make the one thing we most need to change at runtime the one

   134	// Fused read-local telemetry is written only by the physical thread that owns this context.
   135	// INFO reads it with the same exceptional cross-thread snapshot used for LoopSignals and command
   635	    template <bool IofusedPrivateQueue = false, typename Fn, typename BatchBoundary>
   636	    uint32_t drain_task_producer_chunks(uint32_t per_producer_limit, Fn&& fn,
   637	                                        BatchBoundary&& batch_boundary,
   638	                                        bool unmasked = false) {
   639	        if (!per_producer_limit) std::abort();
   640	        uint32_t n = 0;
   641	        auto take_lane = [&](uint32_t producer) {
   642	            uint32_t drained = 0;
   643	            Task task;
   644	            auto recv = [&] {
   645	                if constexpr (IofusedPrivateQueue)
   646	                    return task_in_->recv_fused_private<kInboxSlots>(producer, task);
   647	                else
   648	                    return task_in_->recv(producer, task);
   649	            };
   650	            while (drained < per_producer_limit && recv()) {
   651	                uint64_t age = 0;
   652	                if (task.enqueue_us_low &&
   653	                    sig_.observe_queue_delay(task.enqueue_us_low, age))
   654	                    sig_.observe_oldest_age(age);
   655	                const bool completed_batch = fn(task);
   656	                task_in_->retire(producer);
   657	                drained++;
   658	                n++;
   659	                if (completed_batch) batch_boundary();
   660	            }
   661	            if (drained == per_producer_limit) {
   662	                (void)task_notify_.set(producer);
   663	            }
   664	        };
   665	
   666	        if (unmasked) {
   667	            for (uint32_t producer = 0; producer < nchan_; producer++)
   668	                take_lane(producer);
   669	            return n;
   670	        }
   671	        for (uint32_t word = 0; word < NotifyMask::kWords; word++) {
   672	            uint64_t bits = task_notify_.take(word);
   673	            while (bits) {
   674	                const uint32_t bit = static_cast<uint32_t>(__builtin_ctzll(bits));
   675	                bits &= bits - 1;
   676	                const uint32_t producer = word * 64 + bit;
   677	                if (producer < nchan_) take_lane(producer);
   678	            }
   679	        }
   680	        return n;
   681	    }

   683	    // E0 removes a bounded prefix without advancing the retired frontier. Each source lane is
   684	    // visited at most once, so E2 can publish exactly one retire_n update for that lane after every
   685	    // removed task has reached Executed, Forwarded, or durable deferral.
   686	    uint32_t gather_tasks_unretired(Task* tasks, uint32_t* lanes, uint32_t* lane_counts,
   687	                                    uint32_t& lane_count, uint32_t capacity,
   688	                                    bool unmasked = false) {
   689	        uint32_t count = 0;
   690	        lane_count = 0;
   691	        auto take_lane = [&](uint32_t producer) {
   692	            const uint32_t begin = count;
   693	            Task task;
   694	            while (count < capacity && task_in_->pop_unretired(producer, task)) {
   695	                uint64_t age = 0;
   696	                if (task.enqueue_us_low &&
   697	                    sig_.observe_queue_delay(task.enqueue_us_low, age))
   698	                    sig_.observe_oldest_age(age);
   699	                tasks[count++] = task;
   700	            }
   701	            if (count != begin) {
   702	                lanes[lane_count] = producer;
   703	                lane_counts[lane_count++] = count - begin;
   704	            }
   705	            if (count == capacity) task_notify_.set(producer);
   706	        };
   707	
   708	        if (unmasked) {
   709	            for (uint32_t producer = 0; producer < nchan_ && count < capacity; producer++)
   710	                take_lane(producer);
   711	            return count;
   712	        }
   713	        for (uint32_t word = 0; word < NotifyMask::kWords; word++) {
   714	            uint64_t bits = task_notify_.take(word);
   715	            while (bits) {
   716	                const uint32_t bit = static_cast<uint32_t>(__builtin_ctzll(bits));
   717	                bits &= bits - 1;
   718	                const uint32_t producer = word * 64 + bit;
   719	                if (producer >= nchan_) continue;
   720	                take_lane(producer);
   721	                if (count == capacity) {
   722	                    while (bits) {
   723	                        const uint32_t rest = static_cast<uint32_t>(__builtin_ctzll(bits));
   724	                        bits &= bits - 1;
   725	                        const uint32_t queued = word * 64 + rest;
   726	                        if (queued < nchan_) task_notify_.set(queued);
   727	                    }
   728	                    return count;
   729	                }
   730	            }
   731	        }
   732	        return count;
   733	    }

   735	    void retire_task_lanes(const uint32_t* lanes, const uint32_t* lane_counts,

   741	    // Optional streams A/D filler hint. Visit only producers whose task-notify bit names actual
   742	    // queued work. A producer racing the peek is harmless: the next modulo chunk or the
   743	    // mask-independent idle audit drains it, and this hint alone never controls correctness.
   744	    uint32_t notified_task_depth_capped(uint32_t cap) const {

   747	            uint64_t bits = task_notify_.peek(word);
   748	            while (bits && depth < cap) {
   749	                const uint32_t bit = static_cast<uint32_t>(__builtin_ctzll(bits));
   750	                bits &= bits - 1;
   751	                const uint32_t producer = word * 64 + bit;
   752	                if (producer >= nchan_) continue;
   753	                depth += std::min(cap - depth, task_in_->depth(producer));
   754	            }
   755	        }
   756	        return depth;
   757	    }

   851	    // Sample inbound pressure on a monotonic time gate. The old iteration gate let thousands of
   852	    // idle spins over-contribute zeros and paid a 4*nchan scan on every pass. At most one sample per
   853	    // ~100us makes depth_sum/depth_samples a time-weighted signal without another clock read.
   854	    bool sample_depth(uint64_t cached_now_us) {
   855	        sig_.cached_now_us = cached_now_us;
   856	        if (cached_now_us < depth_sample_next_us_) return false;
   857	        depth_sample_next_us_ = cached_now_us + 100;
   858	        uint64_t d = 0;
   859	        uint64_t inbox_age_us = 0;
   860	        bool inbox_age_observed = false;
   861	        const bool task_consumer = role() == Role::Ex;
   862	        const bool sample_inbox_age = sig_.age_sample_rate && task_consumer;
   863	        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nchan_; i++) {
   864	            const uint32_t task_depth = task_in_->sample_depth(i);
   865	            d += task_depth + client_in_[i].depth() + release_in_[i].depth() +
   866	                 transfer_in_[i].depth();
   867	            // The 100us signal beat already visits every producer scan point. Make that existing
   868	            // periodic full sweep a correctness looker: if a summary hint were ever absent while
   869	            // its lane is non-empty, republish it here. No post/drain branch or extra scan is added,
   870	            // and drain_tasks_unmasked() before park remains the second mask-independent looker.
   871	            if (task_consumer && task_depth) (void)task_notify_.set(i);
   872	            // An empty lane has no age sample. Its retired slot may still carry the previous
   873	            // low-32-bit stamp, so consulting newest_nonzero() here would feed stale/sentinel age
   874	            // into the EWMA after the queue drained.
   875	            if (sample_inbox_age && task_depth) {
   876	                const uint32_t stamp = task_in_->newest_nonzero(i,
   877	                    [](const Task& task) { return task.enqueue_us_low; });
   878	                if (stamp) {
   879	                    uint64_t age = 0;
   880	                    if (sig_.sampled_age(stamp, age)) {
   881	                        inbox_age_us = std::max(inbox_age_us, age);
   882	                        inbox_age_observed = true;
   883	                    }
   884	                }
   885	            }
   886	        }
   887	        sig_.depth_sum += d;
   888	        sig_.depth_samples++;
   889	        if (sample_inbox_age) {
   890	            if (inbox_age_observed) sig_.observe_oldest_age(inbox_age_us);
   891	            else                    sig_.clear_oldest_age();
   892	        }
   893	        return true;
   894	    }

    40	    if (!fused_executor_) std::abort();
    41	    const bool has_unix = unix_listen_fd_ >= 0 ||
    42	                          (srv_->cfg().unixsocket && *srv_->cfg().unixsocket);
    43	    auto run_pipeline = [&](auto pipeline_tag) {
    44	        constexpr uint8_t Pipeline = decltype(pipeline_tag)::value;
    45	        if (epoll_) {
    46	            if (tls_context_) {
    47	                if (has_unix) run_loop<true, true, true, true, Pipeline>();
    48	                else run_loop<false, true, true, true, Pipeline>();
    49	            } else {
    50	                if (has_unix) run_loop<true, false, true, true, Pipeline>();
    51	                else run_loop<false, false, true, true, Pipeline>();
    52	            }
    53	            return;
    54	        }
    55	        if (tls_context_) {
    56	            if (has_unix) run_loop<true, true, false, true, Pipeline>();
    57	            else run_loop<false, true, false, true, Pipeline>();
    58	        } else {
    59	            if (has_unix) run_loop<true, false, false, true, Pipeline>();
    60	            else run_loop<false, false, false, true, Pipeline>();
    61	        }
    62	    };
    63	    switch (srv_->cfg().overlap) {
    64	        case 0: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 0>{}); break;
    65	        case 1: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 1>{}); break;
    66	        case 2: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 2>{}); break;
    67	        default: std::abort();
    68	    }
    69	}
    70	
    71	int run_fused_server(Server& srv, const SnapshotLoadPlan* aof_base_plan,
    72	                     const std::vector<std::unique_ptr<AofReplayPlan>>& aof_plans,
    73	                     const SnapshotLoadPlan* load_plan, TlsContext* tls_context,
    74	                     LateUnixListener& unix_listener,
    75	                     ShutdownReportFinalLine& final_report) {
    76	    const Config& cfg = srv.cfg();
    77	    const uint32_t nthreads = srv.nthreads();
    78	    std::printf("tomokv-cpp: %u unified threads, %u shard(s), thread-mode=1s,"
    79	                " overlap=%u, %s, alloc=%s\n", nthreads, cfg.shards,
    80	                cfg.overlap,
    81	                cfg.net_io == NetIoEngine::Epoll ? "epoll" : "io_uring", alloc_backend());
    82	    for (const ThreadPlacement& placement : srv.placement().threads())
    83	        std::printf("  thread t%u: role=unified cpu=%d L3=%u shards=%zu send=self\n",
    84	                    placement.id, placement.cpu, placement.domain,
    85	                    srv.thread(placement.id).shards().size());
    86	    std::fflush(stdout);
    87	
    88	    std::vector<std::thread> pool;
    89	    std::vector<IoLoop> ios(nthreads);
    90	    std::vector<FusedExLoop> executors(nthreads);
    91	    // ONE boot gate. The ad-hoc mutex/cv gate this replaced needed a separate `runners_stopped`
    92	    // counter so a thread that saw shutdown while parked still reported at the gate (without it a
    93	    // SIGTERM during a long --load hung main forever). FusedBootGate keeps that property as a
    94	    // first-class `gave_up` arrival, and every wait/advance also takes the stop edge, so the two
    95	    // predicates cannot disagree.
    96	    FusedBootGate boot(nthreads);
    97	    // Identical to placement().ifid_threads().front() whenever a unixsocket is configured, but
    98	    // read from the server so the LB's unix_owner_tid_ and the actual attach point cannot drift.
    99	    const uint32_t unix_owner = srv.unix_owner_tid();
   100	    auto report_graceful_shutdown = [&] {
   101	        if (srv.read_local_enabled()) {
   102	            // Joined fused readers cannot run another grace callback. Empty their private
   103	            // retirement queues and disarm every store hook before taking the immutable report;
   104	            // the subsequent atomic-record drain may detach more than a bounded callback list.
   105	            for (FusedExLoop& executor : executors) executor.read_local_shutdown_drain();
   106	            for (uint32_t sid = 0; sid < srv.nshards(); sid++)
   107	                srv.shard(static_cast<int32_t>(sid)).store().configure_read_local(false, {});
   108	        }
   109	        // All owners and readers are quiescent. Release pending-entry references before IoLoop
   110	        // destruction, then return their deferred ScatterState arenas to the correct IO-owned
   111	        // pools. Server normally outlives those pools, so leaving this to FlatStore destructors
   112	        // would leak the retained arenas.
   113	        for (uint32_t sid = 0; sid < srv.nshards(); sid++)
   114	            srv.shard(static_cast<int32_t>(sid)).store().atomic_shutdown_release_records();
   115	        for (IoLoop& io : ios) io.reap_atomic_deferred();
   116	        ShutdownReport report = collect_shutdown_report(srv, ios, executors);
   117	        print_shutdown_report_human(report);
   118	        final_report.arm(std::move(report));
   119	        acl_shutdown();
   120	    };
   121	
   122	    for (uint32_t tid = 0; tid < nthreads; tid++)
   123	        pool.emplace_back([&, tid] {
   124	            if (cfg.pin_threads) pin_fused_thread(srv.placement().cpu_of_thread(tid));
   125	            ThreadCtx& self = srv.thread(tid);
   126	            self.latch_placement(srv.topo());
   127	            bind_thread_arena();
   128	            bool ok = self.init_task_inbox_local_fused();
   129	            if (ok) ok = executors[tid].init(&srv, &self, true);
   130	            std::string local_error;
   131	            if (ok && aof_base_plan)
   132	                ok = snapshot_load_owned(*aof_base_plan, srv, self, local_error);
   133	            if (ok && !aof_plans.empty()) {
   134	                for (const auto& plan : aof_plans) {
   135	                    if (!aof_load_owned(*plan, srv, self, local_error)) {
   136	                        ok = false;
   137	                        break;
   138	                    }
   139	                }
   140	            } else if (ok && load_plan) {
   141	                ok = snapshot_load_owned(*load_plan, srv, self, local_error);
   142	            }
   143	            if (ok)
   144	                ok = ios[tid].init(&srv, &self, cfg.bind_addr, cfg.port, -1,
   145	                                   tls_context, true);
   146	            if (ok)
   147	                self.bind_io_role_hooks(
   148	                    &ios[tid],
   149	                    [](void* p) { return static_cast<IoLoop*>(p)->prepare_activation(); },
   150	                    [](void* p) { static_cast<IoLoop*>(p)->cancel_prepared_activation(); });
   151	            if (ok)
   152	                self.bind_client_registration_hooks(
   153	                    [](void* p, Client* client) {
   154	                        return static_cast<IoLoop*>(p)->prepare_client_registration(client);
   155	                    },
   156	                    [](void* p, Client* client) {
   157	                        static_cast<IoLoop*>(p)->cancel_client_registration(client);
   158	                    });
   159	            if (ok)
   160	                self.bind_client_capacity_hook(
   161	                    [](void* p, uint32_t incoming) {
   162	                        return static_cast<IoLoop*>(p)->prepare_client_transfer_capacity(incoming);
   163	                    });
   164	            if (ok) {
   165	                executors[tid].activate_fused(&ios[tid].ring());
   166	                ios[tid].bind_fused_executor(&executors[tid]);
   167	                if (cfg.overlap == 0)
   168	                    executors[tid].bind_fused_completion(
   169	                        &ios[tid],
   170	                        [](void* p, Client* client) {
   171	                            static_cast<IoLoop*>(p)->fused_executor_completion<false>(client);
   172	                        });
   173	                else
   174	                    executors[tid].bind_fused_completion(
   175	                        &ios[tid],
   176	                        [](void* p, Client* client) {
   177	                            static_cast<IoLoop*>(p)->fused_executor_completion<true>(client);
   178	                        });
   179	                if (srv.read_local_enabled())
   180	                    executors[tid].bind_read_local_demotion(
   181	                        &ios[tid],
   182	                        [](void* p, Client* client, const uint64_t* probed,
   183	                           const ReadLocalFallbackReason* fallbacks,
   184	                           uint32_t probed_count, uint32_t& demoted) {
   185	                            return static_cast<IoLoop*>(p)->fused_demote_local_read_batch(
   186	                                client, probed, fallbacks, probed_count, demoted);
   187	                        });
   188	                if (cfg.overlap == 0)
   189	                    self.bind_fused_executor_hooks(
   190	                        &executors[tid],
   191	                        [](void* p) {
   192	                            return static_cast<FusedExLoop*>(p)->fused_baseline_pass();
   193	                        },
   194	                        [](void* p, SnapshotManager* manager) {
   195	                            static_cast<FusedExLoop*>(p)->fused_snapshot_start(manager);
   196	                        });
   197	                else if (cfg.overlap == 1)
   198	                    self.bind_fused_executor_hooks(
   199	                        &executors[tid],
   200	                        [](void* p) {
   201	                            return static_cast<FusedExLoop*>(p)->fused_coarse_pass();
   202	                        },
   203	                        [](void* p, SnapshotManager* manager) {
   204	                            static_cast<FusedExLoop*>(p)->fused_snapshot_start(manager);
   205	                        });
   206	                else
   207	                    self.bind_fused_executor_hooks(
   208	                        &executors[tid],
   209	                        [](void* p) {
   210	                            // Snapshot's blocking progress loop has no WB filler to interleave.
   211	                            // Use overlap 1's private-lane coarse turn; the main overlap-2 loop
   212	                            // supplies the three-way callback only at its ordinary batch seam.
   213	                            return static_cast<FusedExLoop*>(p)->fused_coarse_pass();
   214	                        },
   215	                        [](void* p, SnapshotManager* manager) {
   216	                            static_cast<FusedExLoop*>(p)->fused_snapshot_start(manager);
   217	                        });
   218	            }
   219	            if (!boot.arrive_loaded(tid, ok, local_error)) return;
   220	            if (!boot.wait_until_ready(tid, self.stop_flag())) return;
   221	            if (!ios[tid].activate()) {
   222	                boot.give_up(tid, "unified listener activation failed");
   223	                return;
   224	            }
   225	            // arrive_ready() returns false on the stop edge: a worker can leave wait_until_ready(),
   226	            // spend time arming its listeners, and come back after main already saw a signal. That
   227	            // arrival is recorded as gave_up so main's wait still sees every thread report.
   228	            if (!boot.arrive_ready(tid)) return;
   229	            if (!boot.wait_until_running(tid, self.stop_flag())) return;
   230	            self.publish_ready_role(Role::Ifid);
   231	            ios[tid].run_fused();
   232	            if (srv.read_local_enabled())
   233	                self.publish_read_local_parked(srv.read_local_epoch());
   234	            self.publish_ready_role(Role::Idle);
   235	        });
     1	// ex_loop.h — the EX stage. Executes ops against the shards it owns; a sender (io in 2s, wb in 3s)
     2	// turns the completions into bytes. Same Channel signalling and LoopSignals units as io/wb loops.
     3	//
     4	//   in   task_in from IO threads         a parsed op to execute
     5	//   out  ready-mask bit / client_in      "you have completed ops to retire" to the FIXED sender
     6	//
     7	// A worker owns no file descriptors, so its "events" are channel entries. It still owns a Ring
     8	// because it needs somewhere to receive wakes.
     9	//
    10	// WAITING IS THE INTERESTING PART. A worker with an empty inbox must not spin a core at 100% — that
    11	// is a real cost at 64 workers and it distorts every utilisation reading a controller might use. It
    12	// also must not sleep so eagerly that it pays a wakeup per op under load. So: spin briefly, then arm
    13	// the blocked flag, re-check, and block. Producers only pay a wake syscall while that flag is armed.
    14	#pragma once
    15	#include <algorithm>
    16	#include <cstdint>
    17	#include <cstdio>
    18	#include <cstdlib>
    19	#include <ctime>
    20	#include <deque>
    21	#include <type_traits>
    22	#include "server.h"
    23	#include "signal.h"
    24	#include "genthread_pipeline.h"
    25	#include "read_local.h"
    26	#include "../net/conn.h"
    27	#include "../net/resp.h"
    28	#include "../net/uring.h"
    29	#include "../net/wb.h"
    30	#include "../cmd/command.h"
    31	#include "../cmd/blocking.h"
    32	#include "../cmd/multi.h"
    33	#include "../cmd/notify.h"
    34	#include "../cmd/slowlog.h"
    35	#include "../cmd/xshard.h"
    36	#include "../persist/aof.h"
