    38	namespace tomo {
    39	
    40	// "Long enough to cover an inter-arrival gap, short enough not to burn a core." A starting point to
    41	// measure, not a result.
    42	inline constexpr uint32_t kExSpinBudget = 2048;
    43	
    44	// How many ops are gathered before executing, so their storage prefetches can overlap. Large enough
    45	// that the prefetches have time to land, small enough that the batch stays in L1.
    46	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecBatch = kGenthreadExBatchOps;
    47	inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalPrefetchKeys = 32;
    48	inline constexpr uint32_t kActiveExpireChecks = 20;
    49	// The armed coarse rotation alternates these two equal quanta. One owner quantum per captured
    50	// producer bounds the stretch before WB by active producers rather than by queued depth, while the
    51	// local quantum matches the most one parse invocation can append for a connection.
    52	inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalDrainChunkOps = kGenthreadIfidBatchOps;
    53	inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalOwnerTaskChunkOps = kGenthreadExBatchOps;
    54	inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalMaxChunksBetweenOwnerBatches = 1;
    55	// Parser-side demotion may reserve one additional point command behind the entire local run.
    56	// Leave that credit outside the pending-read fanout budget so the combined reservation can always
    57	// fit an empty producer lane and therefore cannot retry forever.
    58	inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalDemotionBudget = kInboxSlots - 1;
    59	// Lane ADMISSION pressure window (P128.md). A LANE-FULL deferral arms this many fused rotations
    60	// during which the parser bounds every connection to kInboxSlots / active connections in flight.
    61	// It decays by one per rotation and is re-armed only by the next lane-full event -- never by the
    62	// quota's own deferrals (the actuator must not police itself) -- so under sustained oversubscription
    63	// one rotation in (this + 1) lets the lane prove the pressure again, and once aggregate demand has
    64	// stayed under the lane for this many rotations the bound is UINT32_MAX and the steady state pays
    65	// one predicted byte test per parse pass and nothing per op.
    66	inline constexpr uint8_t kReadLocalLanePressureRotations = 8;
    67	inline constexpr uint32_t kExSchedClasses =
    68	    static_cast<uint32_t>(CommandLengthClass::Count);
    69	inline constexpr uint32_t kExSchedBuckets = kRobWindow * kExSchedClasses;
    70	inline constexpr uint32_t kExSchedBucketWords = (kExSchedBuckets + 63) / 64;
    71	static_assert(kExecBatch <= UINT8_MAX);
    72	static_assert(kExecBatch <= 32);
    73	static_assert(kGenthreadIfidBatchOps <= kExecBatch);
    74	static_assert(kReadLocalDrainChunkOps == kExecBatch);
    75	static_assert(kReadLocalOwnerTaskChunkOps == kExecBatch);
    76	static_assert(kReadLocalMaxChunksBetweenOwnerBatches > 0);
    77	static_assert((kExecBatch & (kExecBatch - 1)) == 0);
    78	static_assert(kExSchedBuckets == 192);
    79	
    80	// Constructed only for an armed declared-key-precise write whose owner has since enabled eviction.
    81	// Keeping the existing maxmemory admission active but forcing NoEviction makes the IO-side promise
    82	// self-fulfilling: this operation can update its declared point/keyset or fail, but cannot delete a
    83	// different key behind a younger local read. The owner restores its live policy before the next
    84	// task.
    85	class ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard {
    86	public:
    87	    explicit ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard(FlatStore& store) : store_(&store) {
    88	        previous_ = store_->script_suspend_eviction();
    89	    }
    90	    ~ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard() { store_->script_restore_eviction(previous_); }
    91	    ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard(const ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard&) = delete;
    92	    ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard& operator=(const ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard&) = delete;
    93	
    94	private:
    95	    FlatStore* store_ = nullptr;
    96	    MaxmemoryPolicy previous_ = MaxmemoryPolicy::NoEviction;
    97	};
    98	
    99	template <bool Enabled>
   100	struct ReadLocalExState;
   101	
   102	template <>
   103	struct ReadLocalExState<false> {};
   104	
   105	template <>
   106	struct ReadLocalExState<true> {
   107	    struct Impl {
   108	        using DemoteFn = bool (*)(void*, Client*, const uint64_t*,
   109	                                  const ReadLocalFallbackReason*, uint32_t, uint32_t&);
   110	
   111	        // A lane entry is the ROB handle only. The full 32-byte Task carried a shard and a
   112	        // scatter pointer that were always -1/nullptr here; at kInboxSlots entries that doubled
   113	        // the lane to the size of the whole L1D. Demotion builds its owner Tasks from the id.
   114	        struct LaneEntry {
   115	            Client* client;
   116	            uint64_t op_id;
   117	        };
   118	        static_assert(sizeof(LaneEntry) == 16);
   119	
   120	        std::unique_ptr<LaneEntry[]> lane;
   121	        // A failed probe can sit behind an earlier bounded demotion wave. Preserve its original
   122	        // reason until that exact ROB op is lowered instead of reclassifying the suffix as Context.
   123	        std::unique_ptr<ReadLocalFallbackReason[]> lane_fallbacks;
   124	        uint32_t lane_head = 0;
   125	        uint32_t lane_tail = 0;
   126	        uint32_t lane_count = 0;
   127	        // Upper-bound owner-task demand for every still-local lane entry. GET contributes one;
   128	        // MGET contributes min(key count, shard count), which bounds its touched-shard fanout.
   129	        // Keeping the sum within the demotion budget makes every task-capacity plan reservable
   130	        // (snapshot pressure may still split it into waves).
   131	        uint32_t lane_demotion_demand = 0;
   132	        // Rotations left in the lane-admission pressure window; see kReadLocalLanePressureRotations.
   133	        uint8_t lane_pressure = 0;
   134	        bool lane_has_tombstones = false;
   135	        bool point_writes_precise = true;
   136	        bool keymiss_notify_armed = false;
   137	        uint8_t reserved_schedule[2] = {}; // preserve the demotion-state offsets
   138	        // EFFECTIVE lane capacity for ADMISSION. The physical ring is always kInboxSlots entries
   139	        // and its index arithmetic still masks with kInboxSlots - 1; this only decides when the
   140	        // parser stops admitting, so lowering it can never overrun the ring. It derives to
   141	        // kInboxSlots and stays there unless DEBUG READ-LOCAL-LANE-CAP sets a test value, which
   142	        // fused_pass_impl copies here once per rotation. It occupies the two padding bytes that
   143	        // already sat at offset 38 between reserved_schedule and demote_context, on the same first
   144	        // cache line as lane_head/lane_tail/lane_count that every admission test already reads, so
   145	        // the struct does not grow, nothing moves, and reading it costs no line the caller did not
   146	        // already own. See P128.md section 8.
   147	        uint16_t lane_admit_cap = static_cast<uint16_t>(kInboxSlots);
   148	        void* demote_context = nullptr;
   149	        DemoteFn demote = nullptr;
   150	        ReadLocalDeferredQueue deferred;
   151	
   152	        void rebind_owned_shards(ThreadCtx& owner) {
   153	            ReadLocalRetireSink* sink = deferred.sink();
   154	            if (!sink) std::abort();
   155	            for (Shard* shard : owner.shards())
   156	                shard->store().rebind_read_local_retire_sink(*sink);
   157	        }
   158	    };
   159	
   160	    std::unique_ptr<Impl> impl;
   161	};
   162	
   163	using ReadLocalExImpl = ReadLocalExState<true>::Impl;
   164	static_assert(std::is_empty_v<ReadLocalExState<false>>);
   165	
   166	template <bool Enabled, uint32_t Capacity>
   167	struct ReadLocalCaptureBuffer {};
   168	
   169	template <uint32_t Capacity>
   170	struct ReadLocalCaptureBuffer<true, Capacity> {
   171	    FlatStore::ReadLocalPrefetchCapture entries[Capacity];
   172	};
   173	
   174	template <bool Fused>
   175	class ExLoopT {
   176	public:
   177	    using FusedCompletionFn = void (*)(void*, Client*);
   178	
   179	    WbEngine& engine() { return wb_; }
   180	    bool init(Server* srv, ThreadCtx* self, bool dormant = false) {
   181	        srv_ = srv; self_ = self;
   182	        aof_manager_ = srv->aof().configured() ? &srv->aof() : nullptr;
   183	        foreign_touch_random_ ^= (static_cast<uint64_t>(self->id()) + 1) * 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
   184	        lb_sample_rate_ = srv->key_lb_signals_enabled() ? srv->lb_sample_rate() : 0;
   185	        lb_sample_countdown_ = lb_sample_rate_;
   186	        lb_controller_armed_ = srv->key_lb_signals_enabled();
   187	        age_sample_rate_cached_ = srv->effective_age_sample_rate();
   188	        ex_sched_enabled_ = srv->cfg().ex_sched != 0;
   189	        pipeline_batches_ = Fused && srv->cfg().overlap != 0;
   190	        // Both interwoven schedules use the proven iofused fixed producer lanes.  The legacy
   191	        // streams implementation remains in this file for branch comparison, but overlap 2 no
   192	        // longer reaches its reservation-aware task transport.
   193	        iofused_ = Fused && srv->cfg().overlap != 0;
   194	        if constexpr (Fused) {
   195	            if (srv->read_local_enabled()) {
   196	                std::unique_ptr<ReadLocalExImpl> impl(new (std::nothrow) ReadLocalExImpl);
   197	                if (!impl) return false;
   198	                impl->lane.reset(new (std::nothrow) ReadLocalExImpl::LaneEntry[kInboxSlots]);
   199	                impl->lane_fallbacks.reset(
   200	                    new (std::nothrow) ReadLocalFallbackReason[kInboxSlots]);
   201	                if (!impl->lane || !impl->lane_fallbacks ||
   202	                    !impl->deferred.init(srv, self)) return false;
   203	                impl->point_writes_precise =
   204	                    srv->cfg().maxmemory == 0 ||
   205	                    srv->cfg().maxmemory_policy == MaxmemoryPolicy::NoEviction;
   206	                read_local_.impl = std::move(impl);
   207	            }
   208	        }
   209	        if (!ring_.init(1024)) return false;
   210	        fused_handoff_ring_ = &ring_;
   211	        wb_.bind(&ring_);
   212	        initialized_ = true;
   213	        if (!dormant) activate();
   214	        return true;
   215	    }
   216	
   217	    void activate() {
   218	        if (!initialized_) std::abort();
   219	        self_->set_ring(&ring_);
   220	        self_->set_wb_engine(nullptr);
   221	        blocking_bind_executor(srv_, self_, &ring_);
   222	        for (Shard* shard : self_->shards())
   223	            shard->bind_notify_pending(&notify_keyless_pending_);
   224	    }
   225	
   226	    // Fused tenure shares the physical thread with IoLoop. IoLoop remains the published wake
   227	    // endpoint because it owns the only blocking wait; this ring still carries persistence CQEs.
   228	    void activate_fused(Ring* handoff_ring) {
   229	        static_assert(Fused);
   230	        if (!initialized_) std::abort();
   231	        // Interwoven schedules put executor-originated task/client handoffs on the network ring.
   232	        // That leaves this private ring with control/persistence SQEs; both iofused-family arms
   233	        // amortize at their shared N2 boundary. Pipeline 0 retains its existing ring ownership.
   234	        if (srv_->cfg().overlap != 0 && handoff_ring)
   235	            fused_handoff_ring_ = handoff_ring;
   236	        blocking_bind_executor(srv_, self_, &ring_);
   237	        if (read_local_enabled())
   238	            self_->bind_read_local_retire_sink(*read_local_impl().deferred.sink());
   239	        for (Shard* shard : self_->shards()) {
   240	            shard->bind_notify_pending(&notify_keyless_pending_);
   241	            if (read_local_enabled())
   242	                shard->store().configure_read_local(
   243	                    true, *read_local_impl().deferred.sink());
   244	        }
   245	    }
   246	
   247	    void bind_fused_completion(void* context, FusedCompletionFn completion) {
   248	        static_assert(Fused);
   249	        fused_io_context_ = context;
   250	        fused_completion_ = completion;

   528	    void run_loop() {
   529	        static_assert(Pipeline <= 2);
   530	        if constexpr (Fused && Pipeline == 1) {
   531	            run_fused_iofused_loop<HasUnix, HasTls, kEp, false>();
   532	            return;
   533	        }
   534	        if constexpr (Fused && Pipeline == 2) {
   535	            // Overlap 2 is the gated three-way extension of iofused.  The old streams loop remains
   536	            // below for branch comparison, but no boot-time dispatch can reach it.
   537	            run_fused_iofused_loop<HasUnix, HasTls, kEp, true>();
   538	            return;
   539	        }
   540	        constexpr bool IoPipe = !Fused && Pipeline == 1;
   541	        if constexpr (!kEp) {
   542	            if (listen_fd_ >= 0) arm_accept(UrKind::Accept);
   543	            if constexpr (HasTls) arm_accept(UrKind::TlsAccept);
   544	            if constexpr (HasUnix) if (unix_listen_fd_ >= 0) arm_accept(UrKind::UnixAccept);
   545	        }
   546	        LoopSignals& sig = self_->sig();
   547	        while (!self_->stop_flag().load(std::memory_order_relaxed) &&
   548	               self_->role() == Role::Ifid) {
   549	            refresh_notify_config();
   550	            // ONE relaxed load per io batch. Per-batch checks are free; this is what buys the
   551	            // per-operation hooks their zero-cost-when-off property.
   552	            if (__builtin_expect(srv_->climon_armed() != climon_armed_cached_, false))
   553	                climon_refresh_armed();
   554	            const bool pause_armed = climon_pause_armed();
   555	            const bool client_cron_armed = !srv_->flip_dispatch_paused() &&
   556	                                           srv_->client_cron_armed();
   557	            const bool client_lb_signal_armed = client_lb_signal_armed_;
   558	            const bool lb_controller_armed = lb_controller_armed_;
   559	            // Placement's dense role vectors are mutated only under FLIP's global dispatch
   560	            // barrier. Do not consult them from an IO pass while that cold transaction is live.
   561	            const bool save_cron_armed = !srv_->flip_dispatch_paused() &&
   562	                                         srv_->save_cron_writer(self_->id());
   563	            const bool client_cron_newly_armed = client_cron_armed && !client_cron_was_armed_;
   564	            if (!client_cron_armed && __builtin_expect(client_cron_was_armed_, false)) {
   565	                // Turning the last client cron consumer off also retires output accounting once.

   567	                for (Client* c : self_->clients()) c->stop_obuf_tracking();
   568	            }

    39	void IoLoop::run_fused() {
    40	    if (!fused_executor_) std::abort();
    41	    const bool has_unix = unix_listen_fd_ >= 0 ||
    42	                          (srv_->cfg().unixsocket && *srv_->cfg().unixsocket);
    43	    auto run_pipeline = [&](auto pipeline_tag) {
    44	        constexpr uint8_t Pipeline = decltype(pipeline_tag)::value;
    45	        if (epoll_) {
    46	            if (tls_context_) {
    47	                if (has_unix) run_loop<true, true, true, true, Pipeline>();
    48	                else run_loop<false, true, true, true, Pipeline>();
    49	            } else {
    50	                if (has_unix) run_loop<true, false, true, true, Pipeline>();
    51	                else run_loop<false, false, true, true, Pipeline>();
    52	            }
    53	            return;
    54	        }
    55	        if (tls_context_) {
    56	            if (has_unix) run_loop<true, true, false, true, Pipeline>();
    57	            else run_loop<false, true, false, true, Pipeline>();
    58	        } else {
    59	            if (has_unix) run_loop<true, false, false, true, Pipeline>();
    60	            else run_loop<false, false, false, true, Pipeline>();
    61	        }
    62	    };
    63	    switch (srv_->cfg().overlap) {
    64	        case 0: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 0>{}); break;
    65	        case 1: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 1>{}); break;
    66	        case 2: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 2>{}); break;
    67	        default: std::abort();
    68	    }
    69	}

   148	    // ---- OUT-OF-BAND FRAMES WAITING FOR EARLIER-ISSUED REPLIES ----------------------------------
   149	    //
   150	    // A retire callback calls back into the loop: cross-shard assembly (assemble_mget stages
   151	    // [array header][borrow][...] into the segment queue and leaves the reply's TAIL in the Op),
   152	    // then the notification/tracking hook, which can synthesise a pub/sub delivery, a tracking
   153	    // invalidation or a MONITOR line for the very connection being drained. At that instant the
   154	    // connection's newest reply is only PARTIALLY staged, so Client::append_oob's frame-boundary
   155	    // argument does not hold and appending would splice the frame into the middle of it.
   156	    //
   157	    // The same parking is also required before a drain when this connection's ROB is busy. Putting
   158	    // the frame straight into the segment queue is a safe frame boundary, but that queue precedes
   159	    // replies which have not retired yet: an SSUBSCRIBE delivery can then overtake its own ack.
   160	    // Each parked frame therefore records the current dispatch frontier and flushes only after a
   161	    // drain has staged replies through that frontier. Frames from different connections, and from
   162	    // different frontiers on one connection, cannot share the old single string.
   163	    //
   164	    // A genuinely parked blocking command is the bounded exception. It is the sole ROB entry (the
   165	    // blocking dispatch is a whole-connection barrier), and while it remains Issued it has no reply
   166	    // bytes to preserve, so a push may take the segment route immediately instead of waiting behind
   167	    // a 30-second BLPOP. Once it is Done, its reply is in flight and ordinary deferral applies.
   168	    // Inside this connection's drain deferral is unconditional because reply staging may be partial.
   169	    bool defer_oob(Client& c, const char* a, size_t an,
   170	                   const char* b = nullptr, size_t bn = 0) {
   171	        if (draining_ != &c) {
   172	            Rob<kRobWindow>& rob = c.rob();
   173	            if (rob.quiesced()) return false;
   174	            if (c.blocked() &&
   175	                rob.at(rob.flush_id()).state.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != OpState::Done)
   176	                return false;
   177	        }
   178	        const uint64_t after = c.rob().dispatch_id();
   179	        DeferredOobQueue& queue = oob_defer_[&c];
   180	        if (queue.empty() || queue.back().after != after)
   181	            queue.push_back(DeferredOob{after, std::string{}});
   182	        queue.back().bytes.append(a, an);
   183	        if (bn) queue.back().bytes.append(b, bn);
   184	        return true;
   185	    }

   754	private:
   755	    // Empty on every serve of every connection that has no subscription, tracking or monitor:
   756	    // one predicted-true test per serve, as before. The drain has finished staging and published
   757	    // its new flush frontier, so every append below is on a frame boundary.
   758	    bool flush_deferred_oob(Client& conn) {
   759	        if (__builtin_expect(oob_defer_.empty(), true)) return false;
   760	        auto found = oob_defer_.find(&conn);
   761	        if (found == oob_defer_.end()) return false;
   762	        const uint64_t retired_through = conn.rob().flush_id();
   763	        DeferredOobQueue& queue = found->second;
   764	        bool flushed = false;
   765	        while (!queue.empty() && queue.front().after <= retired_through) {
   766	            conn.append_oob(queue.front().bytes.data(), queue.front().bytes.size());
   767	            queue.pop_front();
   768	            flushed = true;
   769	        }
   770	        if (queue.empty()) oob_defer_.erase(found);
   771	        return flushed;
   772	    }

   777	    // hot path that moved inlining and cost the split cells ~0.9% of real work (measured against a
   778	    // dead-pad placement control: placement alone was -0.11%..-0.30%, the binary was -0.83%..-1.48%).
   779	    //
   780	    // Every caller already knows the mode statically, so nothing had to be threaded:
   781	    //   flush_ready              carries `Fused` as its 3rd template parameter already, and is the
   782	    //                            path BOTH modes take -> passes Fused

   785	    //   genthread_*              fused-only: run_loop reaches run_fused_iofused_loop and
   786	    //   run_fused_streams_loop   run_fused_streams_loop under if constexpr (Fused && ...) -> true
   787	    // With Coded=false every coded block below is deleted by `if constexpr`, so a 2s instantiation
   788	    // is the pre-reply-code function, not a variant of it.

   790	              bool Coded>

   792	        TOMO_FORENSIC(c.n_serves.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed));
   793	        stats_.serves++;

   796	        draining_ = &c;
   797	        const uint32_t retired = c.rob().drain([&](Op& op) {
   798	            if constexpr (TlsNoBorrow) {
   799	                if (op.no_borrow()) note_zc_suppressed_tls();
   800	            }
   801	            // Cross-shard completion publishes descriptors/state, not bytes.  The connection's IO
   802	            // owner turns those into the final ordered reply here, before the generic staging path
   803	            // inspects the (possibly repurposed) zero-copy fields.
   804	            // Plain commands have no sidecar and take exactly the pre-notify zc_ptr branch. Special
   805	            // command state, borrowed values, and armed notification batches all already use this
   806	            // field, so their retirement hook nests behind that existing test.
   807	            if (op.zc_ptr) {
   808	                if (retire_fn_) retire_fn_(retire_ctx_, conn, op);
   809	            }

   811	                // Anything already staged is older than this op. Once sealed, every subsequent
   812	                // reply uses segments until the queue drains, so no fill-buffer append can jump a
   813	                // borrowed value that is only partially written.
   814	                conn.seal_fill_segment();
   815	                if constexpr (Coded) if (op.reply_code_) op_materialise_code(op);
   816	                conn.append_buf_segment(op.direct, op.direct_len,
   817	                                        op.reply.data(), op.reply.size());

   832	            // direct part so the RESP stream stays in order.

   840	                // thread that owns the buffer. The whole block is deleted for Coded=false, and

   842	                if constexpr (Coded) {

   846	                            if constexpr (TrackOutput)

   850	                        return;
   851	                    }
   852	                }
   853	                if (op.direct_len) {
   854	                    if constexpr (TrackOutput) conn.commit_fill(op.direct_len);
   855	                    else conn.fill_buf().commit_raw(op.direct_len);
   856	                    stats_.direct++;
   857	                }
   858	                if (!op.reply.empty()) {
   859	                    if constexpr (TrackOutput) conn.append_fill(op.reply.data(), op.reply.size());
   860	                    else conn.fill_buf().append(op.reply.data(), op.reply.size());
   861	                }
   862	            }
   863	        });

   865	        bool did = retired != 0;
   866	        did |= flush_deferred_oob(conn);

  1922	    // Exactly one indexed acquire load on dispatch.  The normal optimized build has no bounds
  1923	    // branch; an unoptimized assertion build retains the diagnostic check.
  1924	    uint32_t worker_of_shard(int32_t shard_id) const {
  1925	#if !defined(NDEBUG) && !defined(__OPTIMIZE__)
  1926	        if (shard_id < 0 || static_cast<uint32_t>(shard_id) >= shards_.size()) std::abort();

  1928	        return shard_owner_[shard_id].load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  1929	    }
  1930	    void set_worker_of_shard(int32_t shard_id, uint32_t thread_id) {
  1931	        if (shard_id < 0 || static_cast<uint32_t>(shard_id) >= shards_.size()) std::abort();
  1932	        Shard& sh = *shards_[static_cast<uint32_t>(shard_id)];
  1933	        router_.set_initial_owner(sh.bucket_begin(), sh.bucket_end(), thread_id);
  1934	        shard_owner_[shard_id].store(thread_id, std::memory_order_release);
  1935	    }
  1936	
  1937	    // The caller must hold both executor loops at the safe point described in NOTES-MIGRATE.md:
  1938	    // no executing/retry/group/snapshot work may touch this shard.  Queue entries which arrive via
  1939	    // a stale pre-commit route are harmless because ExLoop rechecks and forwards before access.
  1940	    // Vector capacity and membership are settled while PREPARING still names the source.  The
  1941	    // phase store in commit_transfer() is the sole ownership edge; bucket entries and the derived
  1942	    // shard array publish destination only after that edge.
  1943	    // THE OWNERSHIP EDGE OWNS THE SINK.
  1944	    //
  1945	    // A shard's read-local retire sink names TWO structures that belong to one thread and are
  1946	    // protected by nothing else: the owner's QSBR retire ring (`defer`, a single-producer ring) and
  1947	    // the owner's private block cache (`block_cache`, an unlocked free list). Every armed write on
  1948	    // the shard reaches both through the shard's store, so the sink must name the thread that is
  1949	    // executing that shard's writes -- at every instant, not eventually.
  1950	    //
  1951	    // Moving the shard without moving the sink leaves the DESTINATION executing writes through the
  1952	    // SOURCE's ring and free list. Two threads then splice one unlocked list: the loser's update is
  1953	    // lost, a block ends up linked twice, and the damage surfaces later as either
  1954	    // KvBlockCache::put's `heads[cls] == memory` abort or a take() of a still-linked block whose
  1955	    // KvObj header overwrites the list `next`, so that the NEXT take dereferences a wild pointer.
  1956	    // Both were observed (see DESIGN-P0REPLY.md).
  1957	    //
  1958	    // The rebind used to be deferred to the destination's own next executor pass
  1959	    // (`lb_rebind_pending_` -> `read_local_rebind_owned_shards_after_lb`). Nothing ordered that
  1960	    // pass before the destination's first write to the shard it had just been given, and the
  1961	    // reproduction shows exactly that gap: transfer sid 1 to thread 1, then thread 1 executing
  1962	    // cmd_set on it against thread 7's cache, with no rebind in between.
  1963	    //
  1964	    // Here there is no gap. Both callers hold every executor at the quiesced safe point (the LB
  1965	    // commits only once every EX thread has acked ExDrain, which `flip_quiesced()` grants only with
  1966	    // an EMPTY retire ring), so the source has nothing outstanding for this shard and the
  1967	    // destination has not started. The sink moves with ownership, in the same critical section.
  1968	    void adopt_read_local_retire_sink(Shard& shard, uint32_t destination) {
  1969	#ifdef TOMO_RL_CACHE_NO_EAGER_ADOPT
  1970	        // NEGATIVE CONTROL (Makefile target `rlcache-nofix`): restores the pre-fix behaviour, where
  1971	        // the sink was left for the destination's own later pass to rebind. Every invariant added
  1972	        // for this defect MUST fail against this build; a detector that cannot report failure
  1973	        // proves nothing about the runs that pass.
  1974	        (void)shard; (void)destination;
  1975	        return;
  1976	#else
  1977	        if (!shard.store().read_local_enabled()) return;
  1978	        const ReadLocalRetireSink* sink = threads_[destination]->read_local_retire_sink_or_null();
  1979	        if (!sink) std::abort();
  1980	        shard.store().rebind_read_local_retire_sink(*sink);

   332	    void collapse_empty() {
   333	        if (!rehashing() && cap_[0] <= kMinCap) {
   334	            std::memset(states(0), kEmpty, cap_[0]);
   335	            tombs_[0] = 0;
   336	            cursor_ = 0;
   337	            return;
   338	        }
   339	        release(0);
   340	        release(1);
   341	        cursor_ = 0;
   342	        migrate_ = 0;
   343	    }
   344	
   345	    bool begin_rehash(size_t cap) {
   346	        if (!allocate(1, cap)) return false;
   347	        migrate_ = 0;
   348	        return true;
   349	    }
   350	
   351	    // A moved slot becomes a TOMBSTONE, never kEmpty: the old table is still being probed by
   352	    // erase_in() while the move runs, and kEmpty terminates a probe run. Punching holes made a
   353	    // still-present deadline unfindable, which showed up as INFO `expires` over-reporting after
   354	    // PERSIST.
   355	    void migrate(uint32_t slots) {
   356	        while (slots && migrate_ < cap_[0]) {
   357	            const size_t pos = migrate_++;
   358	            slots--;
   359	            if (states(0)[pos] != kLive) continue;
   360	            const int64_t deadline = kTtlDeadlineSidecar ? deadlines(0)[pos] : kNoTtlDeadline;
   361	            states(0)[pos] = kTomb;
   362	            live_[0]--;
   363	            tombs_[0]++;
   364	            // Cannot fail: the destination was sized for every live entry plus headroom.
   365	            (void)insert_raw(1, hashes_[0][pos], deadline);
   366	        }
   367	        if (migrate_ >= cap_[0]) finish_migration();
   368	    }
   369	
   370	    void finish_migration() {
   371	        while (migrate_ < cap_[0]) {
   372	            const size_t pos = migrate_++;
   373	            if (states(0)[pos] != kLive) continue;
   374	            const int64_t deadline = kTtlDeadlineSidecar ? deadlines(0)[pos] : kNoTtlDeadline;
   375	            states(0)[pos] = kTomb;
   376	            live_[0]--;
   377	            tombs_[0]++;
   378	            (void)insert_raw(1, hashes_[0][pos], deadline);
   379	        }
   380	        std::free(hashes_[0]);
   381	        std::free(sidecars_[0]);
   382	        hashes_[0] = hashes_[1];
   383	        sidecars_[0] = sidecars_[1];
   384	        cap_[0] = cap_[1];
   385	        live_[0] = live_[1];
   386	        tombs_[0] = tombs_[1];
   387	        hashes_[1] = nullptr;
   388	        sidecars_[1] = nullptr;
   389	        cap_[1] = 0;
   390	        live_[1] = tombs_[1] = 0;
   391	        migrate_ = 0;
   392	        cursor_ = 0;
   393	    }
   394	
   395	    size_t start(int t, uint64_t hash) const {
   396	        return static_cast<size_t>(mix64(hash)) & (cap_[t] - 1);
   397	    }
   398	
   399	    bool insert_raw(int t, uint64_t hash, int64_t deadline) {
   400	        const size_t cap = cap_[t];
   401	        if (!cap) return false;
   402	        size_t pos = start(t, hash);
   403	        size_t first_tomb = cap;
   404	        for (size_t probes = 0; probes < cap; probes++) {
   405	            if (states(t)[pos] == kEmpty) {
   406	                if (first_tomb != cap) { pos = first_tomb; tombs_[t]--; }
   407	                hashes_[t][pos] = hash;
   408	                if constexpr (kTtlDeadlineSidecar) deadlines(t)[pos] = deadline;
   409	                states(t)[pos] = kLive;
   410	                live_[t]++;
   411	                return true;
   412	            }
   413	            if (states(t)[pos] == kTomb) {
   414	                if (first_tomb == cap) first_tomb = pos;
   415	            } else if (hashes_[t][pos] == hash) {
   416	                if constexpr (kTtlDeadlineSidecar) deadlines(t)[pos] = deadline;
   417	                return true;
   418	            }
   419	            pos = (pos + 1) & (cap - 1);
   420	        }
   421	        return false;
   422	    }
   423	
   424	    bool erase_in(int t, uint64_t hash) {
   425	        const size_t cap = cap_[t];
   426	        if (!cap) return false;
   427	        size_t pos = start(t, hash);
   428	        for (size_t probes = 0; probes < cap; probes++) {
   429	            if (states(t)[pos] == kEmpty) return false;
   430	            if (states(t)[pos] == kLive && hashes_[t][pos] == hash) {
   431	                states(t)[pos] = kTomb;
   432	                live_[t]--;
   433	                tombs_[t]++;
   434	                return true;
   435	            }
   436	            pos = (pos + 1) & (cap - 1);
   437	        }
   438	        return false;
   439	    }
   440	
   441	    bool deadline_in(int t, uint64_t hash, int64_t& out) const {
   442	        if constexpr (!kTtlDeadlineSidecar) return false;
   443	        const size_t cap = cap_[t];
   444	        if (!cap) return false;
   445	        size_t pos = start(t, hash);
   446	        for (size_t probes = 0; probes < cap; probes++) {
   447	            if (states(t)[pos] == kEmpty) return false;
   448	            if (states(t)[pos] == kLive && hashes_[t][pos] == hash) {
   449	                out = deadlines(t)[pos];
   450	                return true;
   451	            }
   452	            pos = (pos + 1) & (cap - 1);
   453	        }
   454	        return false;
   455	    }

   462	    size_t    cursor_ = 0;    // sampling cursor over the concatenation of both tables
   463	    size_t    migrate_ = 0;   // next old-table slot to move while a migration is in flight

   185	    // Covers every unsealed entry with `stamp` as one batch. Returns how many were sealed.
   186	    uint32_t seal(uint64_t stamp) {
   187	        const uint32_t sealed = unsealed;
   188	        if (!sealed) return 0;
   189	        if (batch_count == kBatchCapacity) {
   190	            Batch& newest = batches[(batch_head + batch_count - 1) & (kBatchCapacity - 1)];
   191	            newest.stamp = stamp;
   192	            newest.count += sealed;
   193	        } else {
   194	            Batch& batch = batches[(batch_head + batch_count) & (kBatchCapacity - 1)];
   195	            batch.stamp = stamp;
   196	            batch.count = sealed;
   197	            batch_count++;
   198	        }
   199	        unsealed = 0;
   200	        return sealed;

   202	
   203	    // Pops every sealed batch whose stamp is below `floor`, oldest first, handing each entry slot
   204	    // to `fn` in retirement order. Batches are FIFO with non-decreasing stamps, so the first batch
   205	    // at or above the floor ends the drain exactly where a per-entry test would. Unsealed entries
   206	    // are never popped here.
   207	    template <typename Fn>
   208	    uint32_t drain_below(uint64_t floor, Fn&& fn) {
   209	        uint32_t drained = 0;
   210	        while (batch_count) {
   211	            const Batch& batch = batches[batch_head];
   212	            if (batch.stamp >= floor) break;
   213	            for (uint32_t remaining = batch.count; remaining; remaining--) {
   214	                fn(head);
   215	                head = (head + 1) & (kCapacity - 1);
   216	            }
   217	            count -= batch.count;
   218	            drained += batch.count;
   219	            batch_head = (batch_head + 1) & (kBatchCapacity - 1);
   220	            batch_count--;
   221	        }
   222	        return drained;
   223	    }
   224	
   225	    // Pops everything, sealed or not. Only valid once no reader can retain a pointer (shutdown).
   226	    template <typename Fn>
   227	    uint32_t drain_all(Fn&& fn) {
   228	        const uint32_t drained = count;
   229	        while (count) {
   230	            fn(head);
   231	            head = (head + 1) & (kCapacity - 1);
   232	            count--;
   233	        }
   234	        unsealed = 0;
   235	        batch_head = 0;
   236	        batch_count = 0;
   237	        return drained;
   238	    }

   417	        // The freeing thread is also a QSBR participant. It has finished this rotation's local-read
   418	        // copy before owner mutation can reach here, so publishing its current epoch is the safe

12:## One-to-one knob accounting
22:| `--read-local-prefetch-capture` | `1` | Deleted; capture selected statically | Preserve the winning immutable-object capture at prefetch. |
23:| `--read-local-atomic-filter` | `1` | Deleted; precise filter whenever read-local is armed | Preserve the winning per-key safety filter, including fail-closed poison and overflow handling. |
24:| `--read-local-interleave` | `1` | Deleted; bounded interleave whenever read-local is armed | Preserve bounded local chunks and per-producer owner quanta. |
28:| `--smt-mode` | `0` | Deleted; derive from complete sibling pairs in the allowed topology | Use existing sibling-unit placement and FLIP invariants when pairs are present. |
29:| `--genthread-schedule` | No independent default; compatibility alias | Deleted | Remove the alias that assigned fused mode and an overlap value. See objection about the original “zero uses” premise. |
38:| `--key-lb` | `1` | Collapsed into `--lb` | One switch controls key and client balancing together. |
39:| `--client-lb` | `1` | Collapsed into `--lb` | Same switch; no independently disabled half remains. |
43:| `--lb-imbalance-pct` | `25` | Collapsed; twice measured quiet jitter | Separate key/client learners; excursions cannot enlarge their own admission band. |
46:| No `--lb` | — | **`--lb 0\|1`, default `1`** | The sole public key/client balancing switch; `0` allocates no LB sidecar, bucket counters/census arrays, or controller windows. |
48:| `--ratio` | Unset; even split | Kept, split only | Global IO/EX counts, spread over locality domains; retain conf/CLI precedence with `place`. |
49:| `--place` | Derived | Kept, derived by default | Explicit `role@cpu` selection remains; fused mode uses labels only as CPU selectors. |
51:| `--read-local` | `0` | Kept, `0\|1` | Effective only in fused plain scheduling; inactive modes retain ordinary owner dispatch. |
55:| `--overlap` | `0` | **`--x-overlap 0\|1\|2`**, default `0` | Study namespace only; same schedules and mode/engine validation. |

  3343	    void atomic_reconfigure_credits(uint32_t window) {
  3344	        // Odd generations close admission while CONFIG takes an exact active-group snapshot.
  3345	        // Borrow/return operations announce themselves so the rebuilt pool cannot race a credit
  3346	        // mutation. IO-local available batches are intentionally discarded by the generation
  3347	        // change; only published active groups survive into the new accounting epoch.
  3348	        uint64_t generation = atomic_credit_generation_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);

  3350	            if (generation & 1) {
  3351	                generation = atomic_credit_generation_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  3352	                continue;
  3353	            }
  3354	            if (atomic_credit_generation_.compare_exchange_weak(
  3355	                    generation, generation + 1, std::memory_order_acq_rel,
  3356	                    std::memory_order_acquire))

  3359	        while (atomic_credit_ops_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != 0)
  3360	            __builtin_ia32_pause();
  3361	
  3362	        uint64_t active = 0;
  3363	        for (uint32_t io : placement_.ifid_threads()) {
  3364	            AtomicAdmissionLease& lease = thread(io).atomic_admission_lease();
  3365	            const uint32_t live = lease.published_active.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  3366	            lease.reconfig_carry.store(live, std::memory_order_release);
  3367	            active += live;
  3368	        }
  3369	        live_atomic_window_.store(window, std::memory_order_release);

  3371	        atomic_credit_pool_.store(
  3372	            window && bounded < window ? window - static_cast<uint32_t>(bounded) : 0,
  3373	            std::memory_order_release);
  3374	        atomic_credit_debt_.store(
  3375	            window && bounded > window ? static_cast<uint32_t>(bounded - window) : 0,
  3376	            std::memory_order_release);
  3377	        atomic_credit_generation_.store(generation + 2, std::memory_order_release);
  3378	    }

    27	
    28	## Capture constraints
    29	
    30	Capture must perform the complete validated probe at prefetch time, not retain only the home word:
    31	linear probing must still skip tombstones and tag/key mismatches, stop at empty, and search the
    32	current table before the old table.  The capture therefore consists of the observed slot address,
    33	the `KvObj` pointer decoded from that slot (or a miss), and the store publication generation.
    34	Execute may read the captured object directly but must not reload the slot.
    35	
    36	The capture is safe only as stack-local state for one bounded local-drain call.  Every such call
    37	runs inside the fused pass's rotation boundary; its `ThreadCtx` tick is published only after the pass
    38	returns.  Writers unlink first and defer both displaced objects and retired tables until every
    39	active participant publishes a tick newer than the retirement stamp.  Thus the captured slot/table
    40	and object remain allocated through execute, while the final publication validation still rejects
    41	an open atomic group, table resize/move, bulk clear, or ownership handoff.  Plain object replacement,

**VESTIGIAL.md — read-only survey**

Audited checkout: `c8e61f646`. Source and history inspection only; no build, server, benchmark, gate, or test execution. No files were written. The pre-existing modification to `CODEX-OUT.md` remains untouched.

The strongest opportunities remove obsolete choices from atomic admission, send handling, and read-local writes. A separate ownership race surfaced while tracing the handoff machinery; it is described after the ranked findings.

Two scope discrepancies matter:

- Fused `overlap` still accepts **0, 1, and 2**. Values 1 and 2 select distinct schedules; the retired implementation is the old streams scheduler. See [config.h:632](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/config.h:632) and [io_loop.h:526](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:526).
- In-place build selectors **1 and 3 remain supported**, and the checkout’s `Config` layout assertion is **528 bytes**, versus the supplied 624-byte lock. See [read_local_settax.h:29](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/read_local_settax.h:29) and [config.h:365](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/config.h:365).

Estimates below describe source simplification and field storage. They are approximate, exclude wholesale deletion of unreachable implementations, and make no throughput claim. Compiler-folded choices are identified explicitly.

**1. SIMPLIFY — Atomic admission still supports a mutable, unlimited window**

Sites: [server.h:2473](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:2473), [server.h:2541](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:2541), [server.h:3311](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:3311).

The live admission and retirement paths repeatedly load `atomic_window()` and handle zero as unlimited. Neither variation survives: boot validates `shards` in `1..256`, then installs `min(16 * shards, 1024)`, always positive. The only subsequent window store republishes the same value.

The link is explicit in [DESIGN-KNOBS.md:30](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/DESIGN-KNOBS.md:30): `--atomic-window` and its live setter were deleted. Nevertheless, `atomic_reconfigure_credits(uint32_t window)` retains its parameter, same-value publication, and zero-window arithmetic.

Collapse to a boot-derived ordinary value, remove the reconfiguration parameter and repeated publication, and make credit admission/return unconditional with respect to window existence.

**Value:** approximately 15–25 lines; four operation-path window-load sites and five associated conditional terms become unnecessary. The credit-generation handshake, lease accounting, snapshot barrier, and live `atomic` toggle still have consumers and must remain.

**2. SIMPLIFY — Serving writeback engines still accept missing infrastructure**

Sites: [wb.h:124](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:124), [wb.h:197](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:197), [wb.h:807](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:807), [wb.h:1049](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:1049).

`WbEngine::bind()` defaults release, retirement, output-limit, clock, and signal hooks to null. Send and retirement paths consequently keep checking whether those facilities exist.

Every engine that actually serves connections is bound by [io_loop.h:104](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:104), which supplies all of them. The sole incomplete binding belongs to the never-serving executor engine in finding 8, retained after `exwb` deletion.

Require complete binding for a serving engine and remove pointer-presence checks. Preserve the actual output-limit enabled value, callback results, and callback indirections; those still perform useful work.

**Value:** roughly 20–30 redundant pointer-presence tests across send/retirement variants, including tests within operation retirement. This removes optionality, not the callback mechanism itself.

**3. SIMPLIFY — Executor-slot translation is an identity lookup**

Sites: [server.h:296](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:296), [server.h:2121](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:2121), [server.h:3508](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:3508).

Boot fills `executor_slots_[tid] = tid` for every physical thread and never changes the table. Atomic, MULTI, and scatter-gather paths still consult it at eight source call sites, including [atomics_glue.inc:217](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:217).

History establishes the obsolete design precisely: commit `3ca2c450e` replaced dense indexing over a fixed executor subset with stable physical-thread indexing for FLIP, but retained the translation table.

Replace the accessor with a bounded identity operation, preserving the existing invalid-thread result. Validated callers can use the physical thread ID directly.

**Value:** 128 bytes of mapping storage, two initialization loops, and one dependent lookup per accessor invocation. Approximately 10–20 lines. This is residue of fixed-role executor numbering, not `exmajor`.

**4. SIMPLIFY — RYOW writes still test for an impossible ring-capacity overflow**

Sites: [rob.h:505](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:505), [rob.h:538](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:538), [rob.h:1012](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:1012).

Both refinement functions test `write_count == kWriteRingCapacity`. Commit-side resolution repeats the test and converts the connection to a conservative generation.

The original ring was independently bounded at 16 entries: commit `f9080c9ca`. It is now sized to the ROB window. The invariant at [rob.h:73](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:73), enforced by the assertion at line 803, makes capacity overflow impossible after pruning: the incoming write already occupies a ROB position that no existing ring entry can occupy.

Remove only the capacity-equality terms and their conversion block. The source explicitly describes them as intentionally retained fallbacks; debug assertions could preserve detection of an invariant regression.

**Value:** three capacity-test sites on armed write processing; approximately 25–35 lines including explanatory scaffolding. **Keep conservative overflow itself:** wide writes and writes with implicit eviction effects still enter it legitimately.

**5. SIMPLIFY — The old delayed retire-sink adoption still runs after eager adoption**

Sites: [ex_loop.h:452](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:452), [ex_loop.h:664](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:664), [ex_loop.h:873](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:873).

Fused passes still inspect `lb_rebind_pending_` and walk every owned shard to rebind its read-local retirement sink.

The deleted protocol is documented at [server.h:1958](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:1958): adoption used to wait until the destination’s next pass. Both current ownership-transfer commits instead adopt the sink before publishing ownership.

The surviving comment calls the late walk a “no-op standing check.” It is neither a check nor a no-op: [flatstore.h:766](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:766) unconditionally constructs `ReadLocalTableGuard`, copies the sink, and advances the topology generation.

Remove the delayed read-local repair from normal builds. Retain it under `TOMO_RL_CACHE_NO_EAGER_ADOPT` if that negative control must reproduce the old protocol.

**Value:** two recurring predicate sites, approximately 20–35 lines, and an unnecessary all-owned-shards walk with generation publications after LB. The shared pending flag still drives notification adoption; that separate path has the correctness issue described below.

**6. SIMPLIFY — Armed writes still support an owner without the now-unconditional cache**

Sites: [flatstore_atomic.inc:1430](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1430), [flatstore_atomic.inc:1451](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1451), [flatstore_atomic.inc:1460](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1460).

Cache take, return, and release-all still handle a null cache pointer. The corresponding sink comment describes null as the pre-cache behavior.

That armed configuration is no longer constructed. **Correctness exceptions discovered during the survey**

These are outside the deletion ranking.

**Ownership race: notification adoption still happens after execution resumes.**  
The LB commit publishes `Idle` at [server.h:1407](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:1407) after moving shards. The transfer updates the read-local retire sink but does not update `Shard::notify_pending_`.

The destination repairs notification pointers later at [ex_loop.h:1858](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1858). Both fused and split execution can drain tasks before reaching that repair: [ex_loop.h:549](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:549) and [ex_loop.h:759](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:759).

A resumed command that expires or evicts a key enters the keyless event route at [notify.inc:427](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/notify.inc:427), which eventually calls [shard.h:166](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/shard.h:166). That writes through the stale pointer into the previous owner’s **plain bool**, while that owner can independently read/write it.

This is a source-level cross-owner data-race path and violates the requirement to move per-owner bindings within the ownership critical section. The later forced drain can recover notification discovery; it cannot repair the missing synchronization. Notification binding needs adoption before resume. This was not reproduced by execution.

**Armed read-local still contains reader retries and topology seqlock validation.**  
[ex_loop.h:1295](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1295) sets captured MGET attempts to two, and [ex_loop.h:1431](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1431) records retrying before the next attempt. This remains live in the default build when read-local is armed.

Default probes also validate an odd/even topology sequence: [flatstore.h:3337](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3337), with writer brackets at [flatstore.h:3494](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3494). Under the supplied prohibition on per-operation seqlocks, that is another contract conflict. These protections currently prevent torn topology observations; deleting them as cleanup would weaken correctness.

**Selectable overwrite variants violate the armed in-place-write prohibition.**  
Selectors 1 and 3 explicitly overwrite published raw values at [flatstore.h:2758](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2758) and [flatstore.h:2784](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2784). Selector 3 also supplies the failed-validation route that can retry point reads. The unqualified selector-0 build retains immutable replacement.

**VESTIGIAL.md — read-only survey**

Audited checkout: `c8e61f646`. Source and history inspection only; no build, server, benchmark, gate, or test execution. No files were written. The pre-existing modification to `CODEX-OUT.md` remains untouched.

The strongest opportunities remove obsolete choices from atomic admission, send handling, and read-local writes. A separate ownership race surfaced while tracing the handoff machinery; it is described after the ranked findings.

Two scope discrepancies matter:

- Fused `overlap` still accepts **0, 1, and 2**. Values 1 and 2 select distinct schedules; the retired implementation is the old streams scheduler. See [config.h:632](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/config.h:632) and [io_loop.h:526](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:526).
- In-place build selectors **1 and 3 remain supported**, and the checkout’s `Config` layout assertion is **528 bytes**, versus the supplied 624-byte lock. See [read_local_settax.h:29](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/read_local_settax.h:29) and [config.h:365](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/config.h:365).

The live admission and retirement paths repeatedly load `atomic_window()` and handle zero as unlimited. Neither variation survives: boot validates `shards` in `1..256`, then installs `min(16 * shards, 1024)`, always positive. The only subsequent window store republishes the same value.

**Value:** approximately 15–25 lines; four operation-path window-load sites and five associated conditional terms become unnecessary. The credit-generation handshake, lease accounting, snapshot barrier, and live `atomic` toggle still have consumers and must remain.

**Correctness exceptions discovered during the survey**

These are outside the deletion ranking.

**Ownership race: notification adoption still happens after execution resumes.**  
The LB commit publishes `Idle` at [server.h:1407](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:1407) after moving shards. The transfer updates the read-local retire sink but does not update `Shard::notify_pending_`.

The destination repairs notification pointers later at [ex_loop.h:1858](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1858). Both fused and split execution can drain tasks before reaching that repair: [ex_loop.h:549](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:549) and [ex_loop.h:759](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:759).

A resumed command that expires or evicts a key enters the keyless event route at [notify.inc:427](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/notify.inc:427), which eventually calls [shard.h:166](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/shard.h:166). That writes through the stale pointer into the previous owner’s **plain bool**, while that owner can independently read/write it.

This is a source-level cross-owner data-race path and violates the requirement to move per-owner bindings within the ownership critical section. The later forced drain can recover notification discovery; it cannot repair the missing synchronization. Notification binding needs adoption before resume. This was not reproduced by execution.

**Armed read-local still contains reader retries and topology seqlock validation.**  
[ex_loop.h:1295](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1295) sets captured MGET attempts to two, and [ex_loop.h:1431](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1431) records retrying before the next attempt. This remains live in the default build when read-local is armed.

Default probes also validate an odd/even topology sequence: [flatstore.h:3337](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3337), with writer brackets at [flatstore.h:3494](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3494). Under the supplied prohibition on per-operation seqlocks, that is another contract conflict. These protections currently prevent torn topology observations; deleting them as cleanup would weaken correctness.

**Selectable overwrite variants violate the armed in-place-write prohibition.**  
Selectors 1 and 3 explicitly overwrite published raw values at [flatstore.h:2758](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2758) and [flatstore.h:2784](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2784). Selector 3 also supplies the failed-validation route that can retry point reads. The unqualified selector-0 build retains immutable replacement.

- The unreachable streams loop and uncalled executor wrappers are dead-code candidates. Their full bodies are excluded from these estimates; findings 7 and 11 concern machinery they left on surviving paths.
- Task reservation remains live in read-local demotion at [io_loop.h:3705](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:3705).

- Atomic-window stalls, cache statistics, and LB movement counters still report varying mechanisms. The established always-zero diagnostic contribution is the executor `WbEngine` in finding 8.

JEDIR    ?= /home/user/Projects/refs/jemalloc/_install
# jemalloc is optional: without it the tree still builds and runs, using the deterministic portable
# size-class table in alloc.h. Set JE=0 to force that path (useful for A/B-ing the allocator).
JE       ?= 1
ifeq ($(JE),1)
  # Prefer the system package; fall back to the copy built from refs/.
  ifneq ($(wildcard /usr/include/jemalloc/jemalloc.h),)
    JEFLAGS := -DTOMO_JEMALLOC
    JELIBS  := -ljemalloc
  else
    JEFLAGS := -DTOMO_JEMALLOC -I$(JEDIR)/include
    JELIBS  := $(JEDIR)/lib/libjemalloc.a -ldl
  endif
else
  JEFLAGS :=
  JELIBS  :=
endif
CXXFLAGS ?= -std=c++20 -O2 -g -Wall -Wextra -march=native -pthread
LDLIBS   ?= -luring -pthread
SRC      := src/main.cc src/net/tls.cc src/cmd/commands.cc src/cmd/glob.cc src/cmd/xshard.cc src/cmd/acl.cc src/cmd/hll.cc src/cmd/t_server.cc src/cmd/t_string.cc src/cmd/t_string_notify.cc src/cmd/t_hash.cc src/cmd/t_hash_ttl.cc \
            src/cmd/t_list.cc src/cmd/t_set.cc src/cmd/t_zset.cc src/cmd/t_zset_ops.cc src/cmd/geo.cc src/cmd/t_stream.cc src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc src/cmd/scripting.cc src/cmd/functions.cc src/cmd/serialize.cc src/snapshot/snapshot.cc src/persist/aof.cc

SRC      += src/cmd/server_tail.cc src/cmd/slowlog.cc src/cmd/lcs.cc src/cmd/info_stats.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/lbsignals.cc
SRC      += src/core/flipctl.cc
SRC      += src/core/genthread.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/cmdgap.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/pfdebug.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/cmdmeta.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/t_sort.cc
LDLIBS   += -lssl -lcrypto
BIN      := build/tomokv
OBJ      := $(SRC:%.cc=build/%.o)

all: $(BIN)

$(BIN): $(OBJ)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(OBJ) -o $@ $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

# The clean string family intentionally excludes the armed instantiations, but its parsed template
# bodies still move GCC just past the default large-unit threshold. 10600 restores the same inlining
# decisions as the base-420b4d492 translation unit; the objdump gate locks cmd_get/cmd_set to base.
build/src/cmd/t_string.o: CXXFLAGS += --param large-unit-insns=10600

build/%.o: %.cc $(wildcard src/*/*.h) $(wildcard src/*/*.inc) $(wildcard third_party/lua/*) Makefile
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(JEFLAGS) -I. -c $< -o $@

asan: CXXFLAGS += -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1
asan:
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. $(SRC) -o build/tomokv-asan $(LDLIBS) -lm

tsan:
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) -std=c++20 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -pthread -fsanitize=thread \
	  -I. $(SRC) -o build/tomokv-tsan $(LDLIBS) -lm

# The armed-write block cache's ownership laws as assertions: the cache and the QSBR retire ring
# are owner-private (one thread, no lock), each cached block is resident exactly once, each class
# list matches its counter, and every shard's retire sink names its CURRENT owner. Debug-only: the
# residency set and the sampled list walk cost far more than the path they guard. DESIGN-P0REPLY.md.
rlcachedbg:
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(JEFLAGS) -DTOMO_RL_CACHE_DEBUG -I. $(SRC) \
	  -o build/tomokv-rlcachedbg $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

# NEGATIVE-CONTROL BUILD for the row above: the same assertions with the ownership-edge rebind
# removed, i.e. the pre-fix behaviour. tests/rlcache_churn.py MUST fail against this binary; a
# detector that cannot report failure proves nothing about the runs that pass.
rlcache-nofix:
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(JEFLAGS) -DTOMO_RL_CACHE_DEBUG -DTOMO_RL_CACHE_NO_EAGER_ADOPT -I. $(SRC) \
	  -o build/tomokv-rlcache-nofix $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

# NEGATIVE-CONTROL BUILD for the cross-owner script reservation sub-wave. Identical to the release
# build except that ScriptPhase::Pin arms nothing, so tests/xscript.py counterexample MUST fail
# against it. A detector that cannot report failure proves nothing about the runs that pass.
noreserve:
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(JEFLAGS) -DTOMO_XSCRIPT_NO_RESERVE -I. $(SRC) \
	  -o build/tomokv-noreserve $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

# Server-less unit binaries: the config parser and the flip controller. `make unit` builds and
# runs both (neither boots a server). tests/gate.sh's parser row is the same program.
build/config-parser-test: tests/config_parser_test.cc $(wildcard src/*/*.h) Makefile
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tests/config_parser_test.cc -o $@
build/flipctl-unit: tests/flipctl_unit.cc src/core/flipctl.cc $(wildcard src/*/*.h) Makefile
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tests/flipctl_unit.cc src/core/flipctl.cc -o $@
# The fused owner's deferred-reclaim ring (QSBR batches) against a per-entry reference model.
build/read-local-ring-unit: tests/read_local_ring_unit.cc $(wildcard src/*/*.h) Makefile
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tests/read_local_ring_unit.cc -o $@
build/read-local-write-ring-unit: tests/read_local_write_ring_unit.cc $(wildcard src/*/*.h) Makefile
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tests/read_local_write_ring_unit.cc -o $@
unit: build/config-parser-test build/flipctl-unit build/read-local-ring-unit build/read-local-write-ring-unit
	./build/config-parser-test
	./build/flipctl-unit
	./build/read-local-ring-unit
	./build/read-local-write-ring-unit

# Load drivers: not part of `all`, kept compiling here so they cannot rot unnoticed.
build/benchtxn: tools/benchtxn.cc Makefile
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tools/benchtxn.cc -o $@
build/broaden-bench: tests/broaden_bench.cc Makefile
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tests/broaden_bench.cc -o $@
tools: build/benchtxn build/broaden-bench

clean:
	rm -rf build
.PHONY: all asan tsan noreserve clean unit tools

**Correctness exceptions discovered during the survey**

These are outside the deletion ranking.

**Ownership race: notification adoption still happens after execution resumes.**  
The LB commit publishes `Idle` at [server.h:1407](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:1407) after moving shards. The transfer updates the read-local retire sink but does not update `Shard::notify_pending_`.

The destination repairs notification pointers later at [ex_loop.h:1858](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1858). Both fused and split execution can drain tasks before reaching that repair: [ex_loop.h:549](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:549) and [ex_loop.h:759](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:759).

A resumed command that expires or evicts a key enters the keyless event route at [notify.inc:427](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/notify.inc:427), which eventually calls [shard.h:166](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/shard.h:166). That writes through the stale pointer into the previous owner’s **plain bool**, while that owner can independently read/write it.

This is a source-level cross-owner data-race path and violates the requirement to move per-owner bindings within the ownership critical section. The later forced drain can recover notification discovery; it cannot repair the missing synchronization. Notification binding needs adoption before resume. This was not reproduced by execution.

**Armed read-local still contains reader retries and topology seqlock validation.**  
[ex_loop.h:1295](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1295) sets captured MGET attempts to two, and [ex_loop.h:1431](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1431) records retrying before the next attempt. This remains live in the default build when read-local is armed.

Default probes also validate an odd/even topology sequence: [flatstore.h:3337](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3337), with writer brackets at [flatstore.h:3494](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3494). Under the supplied prohibition on per-operation seqlocks, that is another contract conflict. These protections currently prevent torn topology observations; deleting them as cleanup would weaken correctness.

**Selectable overwrite variants violate the armed in-place-write prohibition.**  
Selectors 1 and 3 explicitly overwrite published raw values at [flatstore.h:2758](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2758) and [flatstore.h:2784](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2784). Selector 3 also supplies the failed-validation route that can retry point reads. The unqualified selector-0 build retains immutable replacement.

**Tempting cuts that lack the required proof**

- The unreachable streams loop and uncalled executor wrappers are dead-code candidates. Their full bodies are excluded from these estimates; findings 7 and 11 concern machinery they left on surviving paths.
- Task reservation remains live in read-local demotion at [io_loop.h:3705](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:3705).
- Ready-slot exhaustion remains live at [thread.h:1055](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/thread.h:1055), requiring the claimed notification channel and its lifetime protections.
- SMT remains topology-dependent, and `TOMOKV_L3_DOMAINS` remains an explicit environment override: [server.h:164](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:164).
- No confirmed executing residue was tied specifically to `connalloc` or `exmajor`. Current owner-grouped scatter posting still creates one task per shard fragment: [scatter_engine.inc:1246](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:1246).
- Atomic-window stalls, cache statistics, and LB movement counters still report varying mechanisms. The established always-zero diagnostic contribution is the executor `WbEngine` in finding 8.

**VESTIGIAL.md — read-only survey**

Audited checkout: `c8e61f646`. Source and history inspection only; no build, server, benchmark, gate, or test execution. No files were written. The pre-existing modification to `CODEX-OUT.md` remains untouched.

The strongest opportunities remove obsolete choices from atomic admission, send handling, and read-local writes. A separate ownership race surfaced while tracing the handoff machinery; it is described after the ranked findings.

Two scope discrepancies matter:

- Fused `overlap` still accepts **0, 1, and 2**. Values 1 and 2 select distinct schedules; the retired implementation is the old streams scheduler. See [config.h:632](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/config.h:632) and [io_loop.h:526](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:526).
- In-place build selectors **1 and 3 remain supported**, and the checkout’s `Config` layout assertion is **528 bytes**, versus the supplied 624-byte lock. See [read_local_settax.h:29](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/read_local_settax.h:29) and [config.h:365](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/config.h:365).

Estimates below describe source simplification and field storage. They are approximate, exclude wholesale deletion of unreachable implementations, and make no throughput claim. Compiler-folded choices are identified explicitly.

**1. SIMPLIFY — Atomic admission still supports a mutable, unlimited window**

Sites: [server.h:2473](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:2473), [server.h:2541](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:2541), [server.h:3311](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:3311).

The live admission and retirement paths repeatedly load `atomic_window()` and handle zero as unlimited. Neither variation survives: boot validates `shards` in `1..256`, then installs `min(16 * shards, 1024)`, always positive. The only subsequent window store republishes the same value.

The link is explicit in [DESIGN-KNOBS.md:30](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/DESIGN-KNOBS.md:30): `--atomic-window` and its live setter were deleted. Nevertheless, `atomic_reconfigure_credits(uint32_t window)` retains its parameter, same-value publication, and zero-window arithmetic.

Collapse to a boot-derived ordinary value, remove the reconfiguration parameter and repeated publication, and make credit admission/return unconditional with respect to window existence.

**Value:** approximately 15–25 lines; four operation-path window-load sites and five associated conditional terms become unnecessary. The credit-generation handshake, lease accounting, snapshot barrier, and live `atomic` toggle still have consumers and must remain.

**2. SIMPLIFY — Serving writeback engines still accept missing infrastructure**

Sites: [wb.h:124](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:124), [wb.h:197](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:197), [wb.h:807](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:807), [wb.h:1049](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:1049).

`WbEngine::bind()` defaults release, retirement, output-limit, clock, and signal hooks to null. Send and retirement paths consequently keep checking whether those facilities exist.

Every engine that actually serves connections is bound by [io_loop.h:104](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:104), which supplies all of them. The sole incomplete binding belongs to the never-serving executor engine in finding 8, retained after `exwb` deletion.

Require complete binding for a serving engine and remove pointer-presence checks. Preserve the actual output-limit enabled value, callback results, and callback indirections; those still perform useful work.

**Value:** roughly 20–30 redundant pointer-presence tests across send/retirement variants, including tests within operation retirement. This removes optionality, not the callback mechanism itself.

**3. SIMPLIFY — Executor-slot translation is an identity lookup**

Sites: [server.h:296](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:296), [server.h:2121](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:2121), [server.h:3508](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:3508).

Boot fills `executor_slots_[tid] = tid` for every physical thread and never changes the table. Atomic, MULTI, and scatter-gather paths still consult it at eight source call sites, including [atomics_glue.inc:217](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:217).

History establishes the obsolete design precisely: commit `3ca2c450e` replaced dense indexing over a fixed executor subset with stable physical-thread indexing for FLIP, but retained the translation table.

Replace the accessor with a bounded identity operation, preserving the existing invalid-thread result. Validated callers can use the physical thread ID directly.

**4. SIMPLIFY — RYOW writes still test for an impossible ring-capacity overflow**

Sites: [rob.h:505](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:505), [rob.h:538](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:538), [rob.h:1012](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:1012).

Both refinement functions test `write_count == kWriteRingCapacity`. Commit-side resolution repeats the test and converts the connection to a conservative generation.

The original ring was independently bounded at 16 entries: commit `f9080c9ca`. It is now sized to the ROB window. The invariant at [rob.h:73](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:73), enforced by the assertion at line 803, makes capacity overflow impossible after pruning: the incoming write already occupies a ROB position that no existing ring entry can occupy.

Remove only the capacity-equality terms and their conversion block. The source explicitly describes them as intentionally retained fallbacks; debug assertions could preserve detection of an invariant regression.

**Value:** three capacity-test sites on armed write processing; approximately 25–35 lines including explanatory scaffolding. **Keep conservative overflow itself:** wide writes and writes with implicit eviction effects still enter it legitimately.

// op paid, GETs included, for a benefit only coded replies receive. That is the whole of the split
// GET regression. No array on this path, ever.

// The coded reply's ONLY appearance in the per-op retire lambda is a call to this. Rendering it
// inline meant inlining reserve_fill -> SmallBuf::reserve -> grow(), i.e. malloc/memcpy/free, into
// the hottest function the io thread runs -- paid in code size and register pressure by every op,
// including the GETs that never carry a code. Base reached its reply through an out-of-line
// SmallBuf::append call too, so this trades like for like.
template <bool TrackOutput>
__attribute__((noinline)) void stage_coded_reply(Client& conn, Op& op) {
    const uint32_t n = format_reply_code(conn.reserve_fill(kReplyCodeMax),
                                         op.reply_code_, op.reply_ival_);
    if constexpr (TrackOutput) conn.commit_fill(n);
    else                       conn.fill_buf().commit_raw(n);
}

// "Long enough to cover an inter-arrival gap, short enough not to burn a core." A starting point to
// measure, not a result.
inline constexpr uint32_t kExSpinBudget = 2048;

// How many ops are gathered before executing, so their storage prefetches can overlap. Large enough
// that the prefetches have time to land, small enough that the batch stays in L1.
inline constexpr uint32_t kExecBatch = kGenthreadExBatchOps;
inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalPrefetchKeys = 32;
inline constexpr uint32_t kActiveExpireChecks = 20;
// The armed coarse rotation alternates these two equal quanta. One owner quantum per captured
// producer bounds the stretch before WB by active producers rather than by queued depth, while the
// local quantum matches the most one parse invocation can append for a connection.
inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalDrainChunkOps = kGenthreadIfidBatchOps;
inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalOwnerTaskChunkOps = kGenthreadExBatchOps;
inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalMaxChunksBetweenOwnerBatches = 1;
// Parser-side demotion may reserve one additional point command behind the entire local run.
// Leave that credit outside the pending-read fanout budget so the combined reservation can always
// fit an empty producer lane and therefore cannot retry forever.
inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalDemotionBudget = kInboxSlots - 1;
// Lane ADMISSION pressure window (P128.md). A LANE-FULL deferral arms this many fused rotations
// during which the parser bounds every connection to kInboxSlots / active connections in flight.
// It decays by one per rotation and is re-armed only by the next lane-full event -- never by the
// quota's own deferrals (the actuator must not police itself) -- so under sustained oversubscription
// one rotation in (this + 1) lets the lane prove the pressure again, and once aggregate demand has
// stayed under the lane for this many rotations the bound is UINT32_MAX and the steady state pays
// one predicted byte test per parse pass and nothing per op.
inline constexpr uint8_t kReadLocalLanePressureRotations = 8;
inline constexpr uint32_t kExSchedClasses =
    static_cast<uint32_t>(CommandLengthClass::Count);
inline constexpr uint32_t kExSchedBuckets = kRobWindow * kExSchedClasses;
inline constexpr uint32_t kExSchedBucketWords = (kExSchedBuckets + 63) / 64;
static_assert(kExecBatch <= UINT8_MAX);
static_assert(kExecBatch <= 32);
static_assert(kGenthreadIfidBatchOps <= kExecBatch);
static_assert(kReadLocalDrainChunkOps == kExecBatch);
static_assert(kReadLocalOwnerTaskChunkOps == kExecBatch);
static_assert(kReadLocalMaxChunksBetweenOwnerBatches > 0);
static_assert((kExecBatch & (kExecBatch - 1)) == 0);
static_assert(kExSchedBuckets == 192);

// Constructed only for an armed declared-key-precise write whose owner has since enabled eviction.
// Keeping the existing maxmemory admission active but forcing NoEviction makes the IO-side promise
// self-fulfilling: this operation can update its declared point/keyset or fail, but cannot delete a
// different key behind a younger local read. The owner restores its live policy before the next
// task.
class ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard {
public:
    explicit ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard(FlatStore& store) : store_(&store) {
        previous_ = store_->script_suspend_eviction();
    }
    ~ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard() { store_->script_restore_eviction(previous_); }
    ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard(const ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard&) = delete;
    ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard& operator=(const ReadLocalPreciseWriteGuard&) = delete;

private:
    FlatStore* store_ = nullptr;
    MaxmemoryPolicy previous_ = MaxmemoryPolicy::NoEviction;
};
